idea: Direction-only tie with per-token scale and bias
mechanism: Keep the shared 50304x384 table but use its RMS-normalized rows as the output classifier, multiplied by a learned per-token log-scale and plus a learned per-token bias (two vectors of 50304 scalars, zero-init). The tie currently forces one row norm to serve as input salience and as output frequency prior at once, and the 2026 tying analysis shows the output gradient wins that fight; decoupling norm from direction lets the shared direction serve both roles while rare rows (rank 10k+, 11.6 nats) keep a usable direction even when decay shrinks their norm. The conflict is intrinsic to tying and do
prediction: Loss curve pulls below baseline within the first few hundred steps as the bias absorbs the unigram prior, and the gap persists; parameters rise by about 100k to roughly 21.34M; step time within 2 percent (one 50304x384 normalize per forward, done in bf16 to stay under the 0.1 GB memory headroom); th
test: Build-only for the count, 3 steps for time and peak memory, then 45 matched steps against baseline and against the bias-only variant below to isolate the normalization.
breaks: The tied row's norm must encode both input salience and output frequency; this flips it so norm is output-only and lives in two cheap scalar vectors.
keeps: One shared table, plain next-token cross entropy, final RMSNorm, mean read-out, the same Muon and AdamW grouping (the two new vectors fall to AdamW as 1-D parameters).
kill: Mean training loss over matched steps 30 to 45 not at least 0.02 nats below baseline, or below the bias-only variant by less than 0.005.

idea: Unigram bias on the tied head
mechanism: Add a learned 50304-vector bias to the logits, zero-init, carried by the fused linear call. Without it the tied table has to encode token frequency inside the embedding geometry, which pollutes the input side that the same rows feed; a bias removes that burden for free and should give most of its value early, when the model is still learning the unigram and bigram statistics that dominate the first 50M tokens.
prediction: Faster early descent (first 200 steps), a small persistent gain of 0.005 to 0.015 nats; parameters +50,304; step time unchanged; no extra activation memory.
test: 45 matched steps against baseline; also the control arm for the direction-only tie above.
source: port of the classic output bias (absent in GPT-2 and in this script), motivated by https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.26663

idea: Cancel the identity echo before the head
mechanism: Before the final RMSNorm, subtract alpha times the token's own input embedding from the stream mean, with alpha a learned scalar initialized at 1. With a tied head, the embedding component surviving in the residual gives the current token a logit boost of its own squared norm, so the layers must spend capacity suppressing self-repetition; removing it analytically frees that capacity. The echo is a property of tying and of pre-norm residual copying, not of scale, though its share shrinks as residual RMS growth dilutes the input, so the expected gain is largest at small depth.
prediction: Lower loss from the first steps, since at init the baseline's logits favour the input token; one extra parameter; zero measurable time or memory cost (a 384-wide subtraction).
test: 45 matched steps against baseline; if alpha drifts toward 0 within those steps the mechanism is dead.
breaks: The head reads the whole residual state including the copy of the current token's embedding; this reads the state minus that copy.
keeps: Tied table, four streams, equal mean, final RMSNorm, plain cross entropy; the layers still see the full embedding at every depth.
kill: Matched step 30 to 45 mean not at least 0.015 nats below baseline, or alpha below 0.3 by step 45.

mechanism: Remove the identical four-way broadcast: stream s receives the embedding multiplied by a learned 384-vector gate (init ones, so the start is exact), letting streams carry different feature subsets from layer 0 instead of four copies that mixing near identity never separates. Remove the equal mean: read out with a per-token softmax over streams whose logits are a dot product of each normalized stream with a learned 384-vector per stream, so the head picks the stream carrying the prediction. Reinvest the freed redundancy into these roughly 3k parameters. V4-scale mHC inherits the same identical
prediction: Loss curve separates from baseline only after a few hundred steps, once gates and write weights have diverged; parameters +3,072; step time within 1 percent; at the end the four streams measurably differ (cosine between streams below 0.95), which is the mechanism's signature.
test: 3 steps for time, 45 matched steps for loss; log the mean pairwise cosine between the final streams at step 45.
target: residual RMS growth, down, since streams can specialize instead of accumulating four copies
breaks: All four streams must start as the same embedding and be read by an equal-weight mean.
keeps: Tied table, final RMSNorm, cross entropy, every Block unchanged, the stream count of 4.
kill: Matched step 30 to 45 mean not below baseline by at least 0.01, or final-stream pairwise cosine still above 0.99 at step 45 (streams never separated).

idea: Per-position log-temperature on the pre-head hidden
mechanism: Multiply the normed read-out by exp(tau[pos]) with tau a learned 1024-vector initialized at zero, which scales that token's logits uniformly without touching the 412 MB logits tensor. Confidence should grow with available context, and today the layers must encode that growth inside features whose norm the final RMSNorm then erases; a per-position scale restores the degree of freedom at a cost of 1024 scalars. The effect exists at every scale but large models can learn it internally, so the gain is expected to shrink with capacity.
prediction: Learned tau rises monotonically with position; loss at positions beyond 512 improves more than loss at early positions; parameters +1,024; no time or memory change.
test: 45 matched steps against baseline, plus a one-time per-position loss profile at the end of the smoke run.
breaks: Logits need no position-dependent scale once the hidden state is RMS-normalized.
keeps: Tied table, equal mean, cross entropy, rotary positions and every block unchanged.
kill: Matched step 30 to 45 mean not at least 0.01 nats below baseline, or tau flat (range below 0.05) at step 45.

idea: Input-side gradient amplification on the tied table
mechanism: At lookup, use e plus (k minus 1) times (e minus e.detach()), identical forward values but a k-fold gradient on the input path of the shared rows. The tying analysis shows output gradients dominate and leave the table output-shaped; amplifying the input side rebalances the two roles without a second matrix or any optimizer change. This tests the brief's open item directly.
prediction: Faster descent in the first 300 steps where early-layer features matter most; no parameter, time or memory change; too large a k destabilizes AdamW on the table, so a sweep is needed.
test: 45 matched steps at k in {2, 4, 8}; pick the best and confirm it holds at 300 steps.

idea: Low-rank untied correction fused into the head
mechanism: Head weight becomes the shared table plus A times B with rank 32 (A is 50304x32, B is 32x384, B zero-init), computed as one fused matmul over the concatenated features so no second full logits tensor is allocated. This gives the output side its own cheap degrees of freedom, letting the shared rows move back toward input-shaped geometry, and probes the open question of a low-rank untie at a budget where full untying is forbidden. At scale this is the affordable direction, since full untying grows with vocabulary while the correction grows with rank.
prediction: Parameters +1,622,016 to about 22.86M, under the 23.37M cap; step time +3 to 4 percent; peak memory +50 MB for the rank-32 factor and its optimizer state; loss gain, if any, appears after the first thousand steps as B grows from zero.
test: Build-only count, 3 steps for time and memory (the fused form is the pass or fail here), 45 matched steps for an early read, then a 300-step check since the effect is late.

mechanism: The expand matrix keeps its 128 to 768 shape but splits it 192 for keys and 576 for values, giving each head 32 content key dims plus the 32 rotary dims and 96 value dims; wq shrinks to 6 by 64. Keys across all six heads already have rank at most 128, so 64 key dims per head are mostly redundant, while values carry the content that wo reads and gain from width.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters fall by about 74k per layer, under 0.9M total; step time within 3 percent of baseline; validation loss lower by 0.01 to 0.02 nats at 50M tokens, with the gain visible from step 200 on.
test: Parameter count by build-only, a 3-step timing, then a 45-step matched smoke run on seed 0 against the baseline curve.
breaks: Key heads and value heads must have equal width.
keeps: One shared normed 128-dim latent, six heads, decoupled 32-dim rotary path, QK RMSNorm on the content part, full q projection.
kill: Mean training loss over steps 40 to 45 more than 0.03 nats above the baseline's at the same steps.

mechanism: Add a 384 to 128 gate projection and set the latent to norm(W_c x times silu(W_g x)), so the KV code can select features conditionally on the token rather than being a fixed linear image of it. The whole K/V path is currently linear up to norms, which wastes the latent on features that only matter in combination.
prediction: Parameters rise by 49k per layer, about 0.59M total, within the cap; step time up by under 3 percent; loss lower by 0.01 nats or more, with the largest gap on rare tokens whose K/V need context-dependent coding.
test: Build-only parameter count, 3-step peak VRAM check since the gate adds a 128-wide activation per token, then a 45-step matched smoke run.
breaks: Keys and values are linear functions of the normed residual read.
keeps: 128-dim latent shared by K and V and by all heads, latent RMSNorm before expansion, separate q path, rotary path from x.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 not below the baseline's by at least 0.01 nats, or peak VRAM above 5.55 GB.

mechanism: One 128 to 768 expand matrix is shared by all twelve layers, so every layer's compress must write its latent into a common code that one decoder turns into keys and values; layers can then read each other's KV conventions, and the decoder sees twelve times the gradient signal. This frees about 1.08M parameters, which stay unspent to isolate the effect.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters drop to about 20.2M; step time unchanged; early loss falls faster than baseline because the shared decoder trains on twelve layers' worth of gradient, and final loss is lower by at least 0.005 nats if the shared code does not starve deep layers.
test: Build-only count, then a 45-step matched smoke run; also log per-layer latent RMS at step 45 to see whether deep layers push the shared code into saturation.
target: residual RMS growth, down; validation loss down
breaks: Every layer owns its own latent decoder.
keeps: Per-layer compress, latent norm, per-layer q, rotary and wo, head layout and all shapes seen by SDPA.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 more than 0.02 nats above the baseline's.

mechanism: A 384 to 6 projection gives each head a sigmoid gate per token, initialised near 1, that multiplies that token's value vector. The latent RMSNorm bounds every token's value mass, so a token that should not be read, such as a stop word, can only be ignored through the keys; the gate lets it withhold its value directly, which also removes the need to use first tokens as sinks.
prediction: Parameters rise by 2.3k per layer; step time unchanged; first-token attention mass falls and validation loss drops by 0.005 to 0.01 nats.
test: A 45-step matched smoke run; then measure first-token attention mass on a fixed batch at step 45 in both models.
breaks: Every token's value contribution is bounded identically after the latent norm.
keeps: Latent norm, shared K/V latent, QK norm, head count and the full SDPA path.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 not below the baseline's by at least 0.005 nats.

mechanism: Each layer learns one 128-dim latent vector that goes through the same latent norm and expand as real tokens and is prepended as key and value position 0 with a zero rotary part, so queries can dump softmax mass on it without distorting the first real token's key. This is MiMo's and gpt-oss's sink, moved into the latent so it costs 128 parameters per layer instead of a per-head logit.
prediction: Parameters up by 1.5k; step time up by at most 5 percent because an explicit causal mask of T by T plus 1 replaces is_causal; loss lower by about 0.005 nats, max attention logit lower in deep layers.
test: 3-step timing and peak VRAM check first, since the masked SDPA path may change kernel choice; then a 45-step matched smoke run.
target: first-token attention mass, down; max attention logit, down

mechanism: Each head adds a rank-16 correction to its key and value, x to 16 to 64, on top of the shared-latent expansion, as in LRKV, so heads are no longer confined to one 128-dim subspace. This tests the brief's open question of LRKV on a normed MLA latent at this scale.
prediction: Parameters up by about 86k per layer, 1.03M total, under the cap; step time up by about 4 percent; loss lower by 0.01 nats, most of it on recall-type tokens where head diversity matters.
test: Build-only count against the 23.37M cap, 3-step timing, 45-step matched smoke run; sweep rank 8 and 16.

mechanism: Raise the init std of the 32 rotary columns of wq and of the rotary projection from 0.02 to a swept value so rotary logits start at the same magnitude as the RMS-normed content logits instead of about one tenth. Muon updates have a fixed spectral size regardless of init, so the early ratio of position to content signal is set by this constant and shapes which heads learn positional roles first.
prediction: No parameter or time change; early loss falls faster, and loss at late positions improves by 0.005 nats or more.
test: 45-step matched smoke runs at std 0.02, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2; discard values whose step-45 loss is not below baseline.

idea: QK-norm over the rotary channels too
mechanism: q_norm and k_norm cover only the 64 content dims, so the 32 rotary dims enter the 1/sqrt(96) softmax unnormalized: at init their logit std is about 0.09 against 0.82 for content (a 10x gap), and later they are unbounded, so the 22.7 max logits can be carried by the position term. Add an RMSNorm with its own gain on the per-head rotary query and on the shared rotary key, so position and content compete at a controlled scale from step 0, which DeepSeek-V4 does by norming whole query heads.
prediction: previous-token and induction heads form earlier, so the loss at step 100 is lower by about 0.03 to 0.05; final loss lower by 0.01 to 0.02; parameters +64 per layer; step time unchanged.
test: 45 matched steps against baseline, logging the std of the rotary-only and content-only logit contributions at steps 0 and 45; if the curve is not below baseline by step 45, drop it.

mechanism: The rotary projection and the rotary slice of wq start at std 0.02 like every other matrix, but their logits are a dot product of two tiny unnormalized vectors, so Muon's fixed-magnitude updates need many steps before position matters at all. Multiplying the init of these two weight slices by 3 brings the positional logit std at init to about 0.8, level with content, without adding any module.
prediction: loss at steps 45 to 200 lower by 0.02 to 0.04; final gain small, 0.003 to 0.01; no parameter or time cost.
test: 45 matched steps at multipliers 2, 3 and 4 against baseline; falsified if none beats baseline at step 45 by at least 0.01.

mechanism: Early in training the useful keys are mostly local, and a 1024-wide softmax dilutes the gradient over hundreds of irrelevant keys; modded-nanogpt ramps its attention window from 128 up to the full length for this reason. Here the same effect is obtained with no mask and no kernel change: during the first 40 percent of forward calls (counted inside Attention in train mode from the config's step total) the (B,H,T,D) tensors are reshaped to (4B,H,256,D), then (2B,H,512,D), then full, all with is_causal flash attention; eval mode is always full.
prediction: step time down 3 to 6 percent during the chunked phase; loss at step 300 lower by about 0.03; final loss lower by 0.005 to 0.01 if late positions recover in the full-context phase; no parameter change.
test: 45 matched steps at chunk 4 should already sit below baseline (easy win early); the real check is the self-reported loss on the last 256 positions of each window after a full run, which must not exceed baseline.
target: validation loss only, with loss at late positions as the guard

idea: Self-incompatibility: no self-key in the deep layers
mechanism: Shared structure: in self-incompatible plants a pollen grain (query) whose allele matches the stigma (key) of the same flower is rejected, forcing exchange between individuals; here query i and key i are both linear images of the same x_i, and with QK-norm q_i·k_i is the cheapest high logit, so deep heads collapse to near-one-hot self-attention (entropy 0.67), which is a per-token linear map already provided by the residual stream. Instantiation: in the last 6 layers, queries 1..T−1 attend to keys and values 0..T−2 with is_causal, so query i sees only 0..i−1, query 0 outputs zero; no mask tens

test: 45 matched steps with deep-layer entropy and first-token mass logged.

keeps: causal softmax, RoPE, QK-norm, scale, layer count, residual mixing.

mechanism: Shared structure: in a consumer-resource system consumers arriving in order deplete a shared resource, so a patch grazed by many earlier consumers yields less to later ones; here queries are consumers arriving in position order, keys are patches, and P[i,j] is consumption. Instantiation, in the last 2 layers only: S = q·k/sqrt(96), P0 = causal softmax(S), D = exclusive cumsum of P0 over queries, S' = S − λ_h·log1p(D), output = softmax(S')·v, with λ_h per head initialised at 0 so training starts exactly at baseline. Instantiation: k ← k_norm(k) · 2·sigmoid(a_h·latent + b_h) with a_h a 128→1 map per head on the compressed latent and b_h set so the gate is 1 at init; this is a key-side, token-dependent magnitude bounded in (0,2),

test: 45 matched steps; the gate's per-token std at step 45 must exceed 0.05 or the mechanism is inert; falsified if the loss is not below baseline by step 45.

keeps: RMSNorm on q and k, fixed scale, RoPE, causal softmax, values unchanged.

idea: Learned sink key per head, flash-kernel compatible
mechanism: Prepend one learned 96-dim key per head with a zero value, plus a dummy zero query, run is_causal on T+1 and drop the first output row; query i then sees the sink and real keys 0..i. Mass that currently lands on the random first token moves to a key the model controls, and a query with no good match emits a shrunken output instead of a forced average.
prediction: Lower first-token attention mass and max logit from early training; loss curve slightly below baseline from about step 200; step time within 1 percent; parameters up by 6,912.
test: 45 matched steps against the baseline on one seed for the curve, then one 3-step timing; parameter count by --build-only. Kill if steps 36-45 average more than 0.03 nats above baseline.
target: first-token attention mass, down; max attention logit, down

idea: Short causal conv on keys and values before SDPA
mechanism: Depthwise causal conv, kernel 4, on the expanded k and v right before the SDPA call, initialized to the identity tap so step 0 equals the baseline. Keys that already carry the previous three tokens let an induction pattern form inside one layer instead of needing a previous-token head in an earlier layer.
prediction: Faster drop in recall-token loss after step 300; step time up under 3 percent; parameters up by 36,864 total.
test: 45 matched steps for curve parity, then a 1000-step run watching recall-token loss; 3-step timing. Kill if timing exceeds 5.0 s or the curve is above baseline at step 45.

idea: Head split sweep with the shared latent
mechanism: Set n_head to 3 with 128-dim heads, keeping the 128-dim latent and rotary width; the latent is already shared, so fewer wider heads trade head count for a wider match space at 15 percent fewer wq parameters. The Pythia ablation says small heads bottleneck while 128 is neutral or better, untested with latent attention.
prediction: Parameter count down by 442,368; step time within 5 percent either way; validation loss within 0.02 nats of baseline, with a chance of a small gain.
test: --build-only for the count, 3-step timing, then 3 seeds at full budget comparing 3x128 against 6x64; also check 12x32 for one seed only as the expected loser. Sweep range: n_head in {3, 6, 12}.

idea: Unary key salience, a matching-market term in the logits
mechanism: Shared structure: in two-sided matching the surplus of a pair is a bilinear match term plus a type-specific term for each side; our logit is q·k, the bilinear term only, and with no biases after QK-norm the model cannot say "this token is worth attending whoever asks" except through a hacked constant direction. Instantiation: append a constant 1 to each query and a learned per-head scalar c_h·k_j to each key, padded to a kernel-friendly width, so every key gets a query-independent salience. idea: Gain-scheduled temperature from the discarded query norm
mechanism: Shared structure: in control, gain scheduling sets the controller gain from a measured operating variable instead of fixing it; QK-norm fixes the gain of every query and throws away the pre-norm query RMS, which in an unnormalized transformer is exactly the per-query temperature. Instantiation: multiply the normalized query by a gain exp(a_h(log rms_i - b_h)) clamped to [0.5, 2], with a_h starting at 0 so step 0 matches baseline. The correspondence breaks because the schedule is learned and the measured variable is itself trained, so a feedback loop can push RMS up to sharpen; the clamp bounds

test: 45 matched steps on one seed; log the mean gain per head to confirm it moves off 1. Kill rule below.
target: attention entropy in deep layers, down; max attention logit, bounded by the clamp
breaks: After QK-norm every query attends at the same temperature regardless of how confident its pre-norm projection was.

idea: Value heterodyning, position carried on the payload
mechanism: Shared structure: a transmitter modulates its payload onto a carrier at its own clock, the receiver demodulates at its clock, and the residual phase encodes the relative offset, which is how Doppler radar reads motion. Instantiation: rotate the slowest 16 of the 64 value dims by the key's position with the existing rope cache before SDPA, and inverse-rotate those dims of the output by the query's position, so the head's output carries R(j-i) v_j and wo can tell a copy from one token back from a copy from two hundred back. The correspondence breaks because the output sums many payloads whose ph
prediction: Recall-token loss drops earlier than baseline; loss at late positions improves slightly; step time within 2 percent; parameters unchanged.
test: 45 matched steps for the kill rule; then a 1000-step run comparing recall-token loss with baseline. A unit check that rotating then un-rotating at the same position is the identity.
breaks: Position information enters attention only through the logits; values and outputs are position-free.
keeps: The same logits, mask, heads, kernel and wo; only 16 value dims get a zero-parameter rotation.
kill: Mean loss over steps 36-45 more than 0.05 nats above baseline.

idea: Shared attention budget across head pairs
mechanism: Shared structure: in ecology, species sharing a limiting resource cannot coexist on the same niche, so coexistence forces niche partitioning; heads each get a full unit of attention mass per query, so nothing stops two heads from attending the same keys, and redundant heads are a known waste. Instantiation: group heads in pairs, build block-structured super-queries and super-keys so the two heads' logits enter one softmax over 2T keys, making the pair compete for one unit of mass per query. test: 3-step timing first, kill above 7.5 s; then 45 matched steps on one seed. Check that per-head mass share deviates from 0.5 on most tokens.

mechanism: One w_up (the value matrix) is shared by all 12 MLPs while each layer keeps its own gate and down projections; the parameters this frees widen the hidden. In a key-value reading of the FFN, the gate chooses which entries fire and w_down decides where they are written, so those must stay per layer, but the raw value features read from the normalized residual are the same kind of object at every depth; sharing them gives each layer a wider lookup table for the same parameter count, which is how a 2x-wider model gets its advantage.
prediction: At d_ff 1300 the MLP has about 12.5M parameters (2.4M fewer than baseline), step time rises about 7 percent from the wider matmuls, and the loss curve runs below baseline from roughly step 200 onward; at d_ff 1536 (if VRAM allows) the gap widens. Peak VRAM rises by roughly 100 to 150 MB, which is th
