target: loss on rare tokens (should fall, since rare-token memory lives in FFN lookup capacity); validation loss overall.
breaks: Each layer's MLP must own all three of its matrices; the value projection can instead be one matrix read by every layer without loss.
keeps: SwiGLU form, per-layer gate and down projections, pre-norm, Muon on the shared matrix (gradients summed across layers), same init std.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 higher than the baseline's by 0.03 or more (3 seeds), or peak VRAM over 5.6 GB at every width that frees parameters.

idea: Learned gate threshold (one bias, on the gate only)
mechanism: Add a per-unit bias to the gate pre-activation, initialized at zero, nothing else. In this recipe the MLP input has fixed RMS from RMSNorm and Muon's orthogonalized updates keep w_gate's singular values near-uniform, so a unit cannot cheaply move its operating point; roughly half the units are "on" for every token and the hidden behaves like a dense near-linear map. A threshold is the one degree of freedom the spectral update does not supply, and it lets units become selective detectors, which is what wider models buy with extra units.
prediction: Parameter count rises by 12,924 (negligible); step time unchanged; the fraction of gate pre-activations below zero drifts from about 0.5 toward 0.6 to 0.7 within a few hundred steps; the loss curve separates from baseline after warmup rather than at the start.
test: 45-step matched run with the bias logged; also check that AdamW's weight decay (0.1 on the 1-D group) is not pinning the bias at zero. If biases stay within 0.05 of zero at step 45, the mechanism is not engaging.
target: loss on rare tokens (selective units should sharpen memory for rare continuations); validation loss overall.
breaks: A pre-norm network needs no biases; a bias on the gate alone changes what the MLP can represent under Muon.
keeps: Everything else in the MLP, including SiLU gating, width, and init; the bias is zero at step 0 so the model equals baseline at init.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 higher than baseline by 0.02 or more, or learned biases with absolute mean below 0.05 at step 45 (then the parameter is dead and the idea is moot).

idea: Value path reads the previous token, gate reads the current one
mechanism: The up (value) projection is fed a per-channel learned blend of the current and previous token's normalized input, x + lambda*(x_prev - x) with lambda in [0,1] init 0; the gate still reads only the current token. The FFN is the model's n-gram memory, and at 21M parameters much of the loss is bigram and trigram prediction; letting the gate address a value that also carries the previous token turns each unit into a bigram-conditioned entry without spending an attention head on it. Inkling runs short causal convolutions at 975B, so the mechanism does not vanish at scale, though its share of the g
prediction: 4,608 extra parameters; step time within 1 percent (one tensor roll per layer); an extra (B,T,384) activation per layer, about 40 MB total. Lambda grows away from zero in the first 200 steps and the loss curve is below baseline from early on because bigram statistics are learned first.
test: 45-step matched comparison against baseline, against the mirrored variant (gate shifted, value current), and against a whole-input shift (Shift-FFN as published). If the mirrored or whole-input variant does as well, the asymmetry adds nothing and the idea becomes a port.
target: attention entropy in deep layers (should rise, since local lookups move out of attention); validation loss overall.
breaks: The MLP is a function of one position only; the value path may read a neighbor while the gate stays position-local.
keeps: SwiGLU, width, down init, causality (only the previous token is read; position 0 reads zeros), identical to baseline at init.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 higher than baseline by 0.02 or more, or lambda with mean below 0.02 at step 45.

idea: Normalized hidden with a learned per-layer write scalar
mechanism: RMS-normalize the gated hidden over its 1077 units before w_down and multiply by one learned scalar per layer. The MLP's output RMS grows to 10.9 across depth; with a normalized hidden the write magnitude no longer depends on how many units fire, so w_down learns direction only and the scalar carries the magnitude explicitly. This bounds the branch contribution the way Peri-LN does but one matmul earlier, where the norm is over the hidden rather than the model dimension and does not interact with the 4-stream combine.
prediction: 12 extra parameters; step time up about 1 percent; residual RMS growth across depth flattens; the loss curve may start slightly worse (init magnitude differs from baseline) and should cross below by step 300 if the mechanism helps.
test: 45-step matched comparison plus a per-layer dump of MLP output RMS at steps 1 and 45. Control: Peri-LN style output norm on the 384-dim output, to see whether normalizing before or after w_down matters.
target: residual RMS growth (down); gradient norm spread across layers (narrower).
breaks: The MLP may write any magnitude it computes; the magnitude is instead a single learned number per layer and the hidden carries only direction.
keeps: SwiGLU, width, per-layer independent weights, the existing down-projection init.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 higher than baseline by 0.05 or more (allowing for the different init scale), or a layer whose output RMS collapses below 0.1 (the norm plus small scalar has silenced it)

idea: Late-heavy FFN width (Reverse shape) at constant parameters
mechanism: Hidden width grows linearly with depth, from about 646 at layer 0 to about 1508 at layer 11, with the same 12,924 total hidden units. Early layers in this recipe mostly build token-local features that the latent attention then mixes; the layers nearest the tied head must map a 384-dim state onto 50k vocabulary continuations and are where rare-token memory is stored, so they are the ones short of FFN capacity.
prediction: Parameter count unchanged within a few thousand; step time unchanged; the loss curve matches baseline early and pulls ahead in the second half of training, when rare-token memorization starts to matter.
test: --build-only for the parameter count, then a 45-step matched run against baseline and against the Crown shape (wide in the middle). Widths rounded to multiples of 8.
target: loss on rare tokens (down); recall-token loss unchanged or slightly worse as a cost signal.

idea: Spend the parameter headroom on FFN width
mechanism: Raise d_ff from 1077 to 1216 (a multiple of 64, within the 10 percent cap). The FFN is the part with the best loss-per-parameter return at this scale, and the measured count sits 1.93M below the cap. This is the reference gain any other idea must beat.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters rise by about 1.92M to within the cap; step time up about 4 percent; peak VRAM up about 55 MB, which is the risk; the loss curve is uniformly slightly below baseline with a gain of roughly 0.01 to 0.02 nats at the end.
test: 3-step smoke for peak VRAM (must stay below 5.6 GB; fall back to 1152 if not), then --build-only to confirm the count; worth sweeping 1152, 1216 and the exact cap 1230.

mechanism: Replace SiLU on the gate path with ReLU squared, value path unchanged. At a 50M-token budget the sparser, convex gate trains the FFN as a more clearly addressable memory, and Primer's search found the squared activation to be the single largest gain; the open question is whether it holds inside a gated form at this size, which the 1.3B tie leaves unanswered.
prediction: Parameter count and step time unchanged; the MLP output is much smaller at init (squares of small pre-activations), so the first 50 steps are slightly worse, after which the curve should cross below baseline if the sparsity helps; hidden activity falls to about 20 to 30 percent of units per token.
test: 45-step matched run against baseline and against plain ReLU gating (ReGLU), to separate "sparse" from "squared". If both fall behind baseline at step 45 by more than noise, discard.
target: loss on rare tokens (down if the sparser memory specializes); validation loss overall.

mechanism: For any doubly-stochastic M, 1ᵀM = 1ᵀ, so the stream-sum evolves as a plain single residual stream and the final mean read is invariant to every learned mixing matrix; whatever the 3-dim stream-difference subspace learns is only ever used by in-block reads, never by the head. Replace the final mean with a learned 4-vector read, initialized one-hot on stream 0 (identical to the mean at init since the streams start as copies), with signs free, so the composed transport plan of all 24 mixing stages now determines what the head sees and the mixing logits receive a direct output gradient.
prediction: Loss curve equal at step 1, diverging downward after the streams separate (step 100 onward); +4 parameters; step time unchanged; the final 4×384 stream state is saved once for backward (13 MB).
test: 3-step timing and a 45-step matched smoke run against the baseline curve; print the learned read vector and the per-stream RMS at the end to confirm it moved off one-hot.
target: residual RMS growth (the signed read can subtract the dominant stream) and validation loss only
breaks: the head reads the uniform mean of the streams, which is provably independent of all mixing matrices.
keeps: four streams, static doubly-stochastic 4×4 Sinkhorn mixes, softmax reads, sigmoid writes, final RMSNorm, tied head.
kill: mean train loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.03 above the baseline's at the same steps.

mechanism: The brief says Sinkhorn mixing "bounds residual growth" yet RMS grows 7.8x; literalized, mixing is a mass-conserving transport, so all growth comes from the writes, which are outside the constraint. Make the branch output a fifth input stream and apply one 5×5 Sinkhorn matrix per stage to [x₁..x₄, branch], keeping the first four rows: each new stream is a convex combination of old streams and the branch, so the residual is an exponential moving average rather than a sum, RMS is bounded by the largest branch norm, and every block's output reaches the head with a comparable weight instead of the
prediction: Residual RMS growth drops from 7.8x to near 1x; parameter count +10 per block (2×25 logits replace 2×16 plus 8 write logits), +120 total; step time within 1% (same Sinkhorn loop on a 5×5); initial loss curve slightly slower for the first 20 steps if the branch column is initialized to a running-mean
test: Parameter count by --build-only, a 3-step timing, then a 45-step matched smoke run; log the stream RMS at the last block to confirm it is bounded.
target: residual RMS growth, down; gradient norm spread across depth, down
breaks: a write adds the branch to the residual with a gain near 1, so the residual norm accumulates with depth.
keeps: four streams, static doubly-stochastic Sinkhorn mixing (now 5×5), token-independent softmax reads, 20 iterations, mean output read.
kill: mean train loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.08 above the baseline's, or step-45 loss not below step-20 loss.

idea: Streams as depth buckets with an embedding reservoir
mechanism: Literalize the brief's "four-stream residual ≈ embedding/U-net skips": a stream that no block writes to is exactly a clean embedding skip available to every read, and a stream written only by one depth-quarter is exactly one bucket of Kimi's Attention Residuals. Initialize the write logits so stream 0 receives no writes (logit about -6, gain near 0.005) and streams 1-3 receive writes from blocks 0-3, 4-7 and 8-11 respectively with gain 1 (others near 0), keep the identity Sinkhorn init; the read softmax at every block can then pull the raw embedding, the early-depth sum or the late-depth sum s
prediction: Zero parameter change, zero step-time change; read weights move off uniform within 100 steps; loss curve below baseline from the mid-run onward; the output mean becomes (embedding + 3 depth-bucket sums)/4, so the final norm scale shifts but is learned.
test: 45-step matched smoke run; dump the softmax read weights per block to confirm late blocks read the early and embedding buckets with non-uniform weight.
target: loss on rare tokens, down (clean embedding reachable at depth); residual RMS growth, down (writes spread over three streams)
breaks: every stage writes its branch into all four streams with gains near 1.
keeps: four streams, static doubly-stochastic mixing with 20 Sinkhorn iterations, softmax reads, sigmoid writes (only the init moves), mean output read.
kill: mean train loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.03 above the baseline's.

idea: Decay anchored at the init, not at uniform mixing
mechanism: Sinkhorn on exp(L) is invariant to L shifted by row and column constants, and AdamW's decay shrinks L toward zero, which is the uniform 1/4 matrix: the optimizer regularizes every mixing stage toward full stream collapse, and shrinks write and read logits toward perfect symmetry, undoing the deliberate asymmetric init. Reparameterize each logit tensor as a fixed buffer holding the init plus a learned zero-initialized delta, so decay pulls toward the identity mix and asymmetric writes instead of toward uniform; the optimizer code is untouched.
prediction: Identical loss at step 1; mixing diagonal stays at 0.99 instead of drifting toward 0.9 by mid-run; same parameter count and step time; a small late-run gain as streams keep their separation under cooldown.
test: Print the Sinkhorn diagonal of block 6 at step 45 for baseline and candidate (the baseline's should already have dropped by lr×wd×45 = 4%); then a 45-step matched smoke run and a full 3-seed run, since the effect is cumulative.
target: residual RMS growth, down (less uniform mixing of a dominant stream); validation loss only
breaks: the regularizer's zero point is the origin of the logit parameterization, which under Sinkhorn is uniform mixing.
keeps: everything about the forward computation, the optimizer and its hyperparameters.
kill: Sinkhorn diagonal of the candidate differs from the baseline's by less than 0.005 at step 45 (then decay was never the drift mechanism), or train loss over steps 41-45 is more than 0.02 above baseline

idea: Per-stream RMS before the convex read
mechanism: A softmax read is a selector only if streams have equal norm; with RMS growth concentrated in the written stream, the read is dominated by the loudest stream regardless of the weights, so read logits get almost no useful gradient. Divide each stream by its own RMS (a (B,T,4,1) tensor, cheap to save) inside the read, fold w_i/rms_i into one weight tensor and keep n1/n2 afterwards unchanged, so the read weights become a real per-stream selection.
prediction: Zero parameters added; under 1% step time; memory +0.4 MB per stage; read weights depart from uniform earlier and further; loss curve slightly below baseline after the first few hundred steps.
test: 3-step timing and peak-VRAM check (must stay under 5.6 GB), then a 45-step matched smoke run; log read weight entropy per block.
target: gradient norm spread across depth, down; validation loss only
breaks: the read is a convex combination of raw, unnormalized streams.
keeps: four streams, static Sinkhorn mixing, token-independent softmax read weights, sigmoid writes, pre-branch RMSNorm.
kill: mean train loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.02 above the baseline's, or peak VRAM above 5.6 GB.

mechanism: The current write init gives gains of 1.015 versus 0.995 across streams, which is symmetric to within 2%, so the streams remain near-copies and the mixing has nothing to mix; Hyper-Connections initialize each stage's write to a single stream, and the stream-collapse paper shows symmetry-breaking init reduces one-stream dominance. Initialize write logits so stage s of block ℓ writes with gain 1 to stream (2ℓ+s) mod 4 and gain about 0.02 to the others (logit -4.6).
prediction: No parameter or time change; per-stream RMS becomes balanced (four streams of similar norm instead of one dominant); loss curve matches baseline early and ends 0.005 to 0.01 lower.
test: 45-step matched smoke run plus the stream RMS printout; the full 3-seed run decides.

mechanism: The 6.0 identity init gives off-diagonal entries of 0.0025 after Sinkhorn, so cross-stream exchange is effectively zero and the sHC finding that mHC matrices sit at identity holds from step 0 by construction; a lower init lets each stage diffuse a controlled fraction of each stream into the others, which is the only route by which stream differences created by the writes reach other reads.
prediction: Lower init raises the fraction of a write visible in other streams after one stage from 0.75% to 10-30%; the loss curve changes little in the first 100 steps and improves late if any exchange is useful; no parameter or time change.
test: Sweep mix_logits init over {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 6.0} in 45-step smoke runs, then the two best at full length over 3 seeds.
target: residual RMS growth, down (diffusion spreads the dominant stream); validation loss only

idea: Embedding RMSNorm (input scale decoupled from the tied head)
mechanism: Add an RMSNorm with learned gain directly after the token lookup, so every token enters the four streams at unit RMS. With tied embeddings the row norms of E are set by the head gradient and AdamW decay, so rare tokens enter at a fraction of the scale of frequent ones and are drowned by the first branch writes; the norm removes that coupling without touching the head.
prediction: First 50 steps slightly slower (branches start at 1.6% of the stream), then lower loss, concentrated on rare tokens. +384 params, step time unchanged.
test: 45-step smoke matched against baseline; then a 200-step run comparing loss on tokens below rank 5,000 in frequency.

idea: QK-norm gain init above 1 (uncapping the attention logit)
mechanism: After QK RMSNorm the content logit is bounded by 64*g_q*g_k/sqrt(96) = 6.5 at gain 1, and the gains must grow under AdamW at 3e-3 per step against decay 0.1 before any head can attend sharply over 1024 positions. Initializing the q and k norm gains at g > 1 gives the sharp regime from step 0 (the speedrun found 1.36x the default scale optimal after QK-norm).
prediction: Faster drop in the first 300 steps, higher max attention logit, lower deep-layer attention entropy, final loss lower by a few hundredths of a nat. No param or time change.
test: 45-step smoke at g in {1, 1.5, 2}; kill a value if its step-45 loss is above baseline. Full 3-seed run on the best.
target: max attention logit, up; attention entropy in deep layers, down

idea: Final-norm gain at zero (zero-init head through the tie)
mechanism: The head is tied so it cannot be zero-initialized, but logits = gain * x_hat * E, so a final-norm gain of 0 gives uniform logits at step 0. Both Muon and Adam are scale-invariant to gradient magnitude, so the body trains at full speed while the gain grows, and the soft early targets remove the noise the random 0.39-std logits inject into the first hundred updates.
prediction: Step-0 loss exactly ln(50304); by step 45 below baseline; final loss lower by 0.01 to 0.02. No param or time change.
test: 45-step smoke at gain init in {0, 0.1, 0.3}; the body's gradient is zero for exactly one step at 0, so compare from step 5.

mechanism: A 384x384 Gaussian at std 0.02 has spectral norm 0.78 while a Muon step has spectral norm 0.02, so the random dominant directions survive for roughly 40 steps and afterward decay only through weight decay, lingering as a 10% random component at the end. Shrinking the input-projection init (wq, compress, expand, rotary, w_gate, w_up) to std 0.01 or 0.005 halves the junk without changing the branch scaling.
prediction: Identical first 10 steps, then a small persistent gap in favor of the smaller init; no change in params or time.
test: 45-step and 200-step smoke at std in {0.02, 0.01, 0.005}; kill if 0.005 is worse than 0.02 at step 200.

idea: Multi-timescale streams (subtract the identical copies, reinvest in graded write rates)
mechanism: Removal: the near-symmetric write start, which keeps all four streams within 2% of each other so three of them are copies that cost memory and buy nothing. Reinvestment: initialize the write logits so the streams receive each branch at weights 1.6, 0.8, 0.4, 0.2, making stream 3 a slow near-embedding channel and stream 0 a fast accumulator, so each layer's read softmax can choose between recent and ancient state, the same role the Attention Residuals of Kimi K3 play without their cost.
prediction: Per-stream RMS diverges within 100 steps; read softmaxes leave uniform; loss gain appears after step 300. 0 extra params, unchanged time.
test: 45-step smoke; then at 200 steps check the per-stream RMS ratio (kill if still within 1.2x) and the matched loss.
target: residual RMS growth, spread across streams up; validation loss down
breaks: The four residual streams start as, and remain, interchangeable copies.
keeps: Sinkhorn mixing, softmax reads, mean-of-streams at the head, scaled branch init, pre-norm on the collapsed read-out.
kill: step-45 matched loss above baseline by more than 0.02.

idea: No-affine norms with one scalar temperature each (subtract the gain vectors)
mechanism: Removal: every per-channel norm gain (9,600 params), which modded-nanogpt shows are unnecessary and which AdamW decay pulls toward zero all run. Reinvestment: each norm keeps a single scalar, initialized so the attention temperature starts at 1.4x and the MLP gate pre-activation at the current scale, because these two temperatures are the only scales Muon's uniform-singular-value updates cannot set cheaply.
prediction: Loss within 0.01 of baseline through step 100, then lower because the temperatures are no longer fighting decay channel by channel. Params down 9,560.
test: 45-step smoke; a 500-step run comparing the gain vector's channel spread in the baseline (if the baseline gains stay within 10% of uniform, the vector was idle and the removal is safe).
breaks: Each normalization owns a learned per-channel gain.
keeps: Pre-norm placement, RMS statistic, QK-norm, scaled init, all branch shapes.
kill: step-45 matched loss above baseline by more than 0.03.

idea: Magnitude-aware head temperature (subtract scale-freeness at the final norm)
mechanism: Removal: the final RMSNorm throws away the residual magnitude, so a token whose residual grew large from many confident writes gets the same logit temperature as one the layers barely touched. Reinvestment: multiply the final normalized output by exp(a * (log RMS - m)) with scalars a (init 0) and m, so the model can sharpen confident tokens and hedge uncertain ones. The null case is exactly the baseline.
prediction: a drifts positive within a few hundred steps; the loss gap is calibration-sized, 0.005 to 0.01. +2 params, unchanged time.
test: Pre-check on the baseline: correlation between per-token final-residual RMS and per-token loss over 2M tokens; kill if |corr| < 0.1 without training. Then a 45-step smoke.
breaks: The head's logit temperature is independent of the residual magnitude.
keeps: RMS normalization, tied head, cross-entropy, all layers unchanged.
kill: step-45 matched loss above baseline by more than 0.01.

idea: Grouped RMS statistic on the read-out (subtract the single per-token statistic)
mechanism: Removal: the one RMS per token, which lets a few outlier channels of the kind that form around attention sinks dominate the divisor and silence the other 380 channels for that token. Reinvestment: six groups of 64 channels each normalized by their own RMS in n1, n2 and the final norm, so an outlier group cannot rescale the rest, at the cost of six reductions instead of one.
prediction: Lower first-token attention mass in deep layers and a loss gain at late positions; params unchanged, step time within 2%.
test: Pre-check on the baseline: max |channel| over RMS of the read-out in layers 6 to 11; kill without training if below 5. Then a 45-step smoke.
breaks: Normalization uses one statistic per token.
keeps: Pre-norm on the collapsed read-out, learned gains, scaled init, all shapes.
kill: step-45 matched loss above baseline by more than 0.02.

mechanism: Initialize each stage's mixing logits at a cyclic shift instead of the identity and write the branch output only into the slot that the shift just vacated; stream j then holds the residual state exactly j stages back, so a layer's softmax read can form differences of consecutive states, which are the last three branch outputs individually, at zero added cost. This is a four-deep DenseFormer window built from parts the model already pays for, and the uniform read still equals the plain residual sum because each write lands in exactly one slot and is never lost.
prediction: Parameter count unchanged, step time unchanged within noise; train loss matches the baseline for the first 100 steps and pulls ahead by 0.02 to 0.04 nats by step 400 as the read weights move off uniform.
test: A 45-step seed-matched smoke run against the baseline, then a 300-step run; also dump the learned read weights per stage at the end to confirm they left the uniform 0.25 (the baseline's should still sit near 0.25, which is the diagnostic that the baseline's streams never differentiate).
breaks: Stream k after a stage equals stream k before it plus the write; stream identity persists across depth.
keeps: Twelve sequential blocks, the Sinkhorn parametrization, the read and write gates, the mean readout, the optimizer split.
kill: Step-45 train loss more than 0.03 nats above the baseline's step-45 loss on the same seed.

mechanism: Change only the write-gate init so stage s of block l writes with weight near 1.9 into stream (2l+s) mod 4 and near 0.1 into the others; the four streams become sums over four interleaved depth bands instead of four near-identical copies. The baseline's 0.03 versus minus 0.01 start gives write weights of 1.015 versus 0.995, so its streams receive identical gradients and the whole four-stream apparatus, the Sinkhorn included, is a cost paid for nothing; breaking the symmetry at init is the cheapest way to make it earn its memory.
prediction: Parameter count and step time unchanged; per-stream RMS at the top of the stack drops to about half the baseline's; loss curve equal to the baseline through warmup and lower by 0.01 to 0.03 nats by step 500.
test: Sweep the own-stream logit over 1, 2 and 3 and the off-stream logit over minus 3 and minus 1 at 45 matched steps, with the baseline as a sixth arm; discard any setting that is above the baseline at step 45.

idea: Second pass over the middle blocks with pass-specific stream logits
mechanism: Blocks 4 to 9 are applied twice, so the model spends 18 block applications per token on 12 blocks' weights, and the only new parameters are a second set of mix, read and write logits for the second pass, 56 per block. The stream logits act as the per-loop adapters of relaxed recursive transformers for free, and at 2.4 tokens per parameter the budget is data-limited, so more compute per token with the same weights should buy loss where more weights would not. The looped applications are wrapped in activation checkpointing to stay under 5.6 GB.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters up by 336; step time about 1.45 times the baseline, near 6.9 s; peak VRAM within 0.1 GB of the baseline because of the checkpointing; train loss slightly worse than the baseline until about step 100, then 0.03 to 0.06 nats better by step 500.
test: A 3-step timing and peak-memory check first; then a 45-step matched smoke run, then 300 steps. A variant that loops blocks 8 to 11 instead distinguishes "more depth helps" from "mid-stack refinement helps".
breaks: Every block is applied exactly once per forward pass.
keeps: Twelve unique blocks, their order, the stream machinery, the optimizer and schedule.
kill: Step-45 train loss more than 0.05 nats above the baseline's, or peak VRAM above 5.6 GB in the 3-step check.

idea: Progressive stacking from six to twelve blocks
mechanism: For the first quarter of the steps only blocks 0 to 5 run; at the growth step the model copies each of them into block 6 to 11 and the loop switches to all twelve. The shallow phase learns the unigram and bigram structure at 0.7 times the step cost and a steeper per-token slope, and the copied stack starts from a trained function rather than a cold one, which the stacking literature reports as 1.5 to 2 times token efficiency.
prediction: Parameter count unchanged; first-phase steps about 0.7 times the baseline's time, full-phase unchanged; a loss bump of under 0.1 nats at the growth step that recovers within 50 steps, and a curve 0.02 to 0.04 nats below the baseline by the start of cooldown.
test: Run with growth at step 100 for a 300-step budget and compare the matched-step curve; if the post-growth loss is still above the baseline at step 300 the idea dies. The growth step fraction is the one constant to sweep, over 0.15, 0.25 and 0.4.

mechanism: In the last three blocks attention and MLP read the same normalized state and run in parallel, and each writes into its own stream instead of into the same residual, so the two branches cannot cancel and the next stage's read can weight them separately. The redundancy profile of deep layers says late blocks are near-identity, so sequential ordering there buys little; the parallel layout also drops one Sinkhorn, one read and one combine per block, which lowers step time and activation memory.
prediction: Parameters unchanged; step time down about 4 percent and peak VRAM down about 0.15 GB; loss curve within 0.01 nats of the baseline at matched steps, with the win, if any, under 0.02 nats.
test: A 45-step matched smoke run plus a 3-step memory check; a second arm applies the layout to the first three blocks instead, which the mechanism predicts should hurt.
source: own (tests the open item from https://arxiv.org/html/2502.05795v3)
target: attention entropy in deep layers, down
breaks: Every block is one attention stage followed by one MLP stage.
keeps: Block count, parameters, the stream mixing in the first nine blocks, the optimizer.
kill: Step-45 train loss more than 0.02 nats above the baseline's.

mechanism: Each stage multiplies its branch output by a sigmoid of a learned vector dotted with the normalized stage input, with a bias so the gate starts at 0.95; the gate vector is 1-D so it falls to AdamW. Easy tokens can then damp late-layer writes that add noise to a prediction already made, and the model's late-layer capacity concentrates on hard tokens without any routing, skipping or lost KV entries.
prediction: Parameters up by 9,240; step time unchanged within noise; the gate distribution bimodalizes by step 300, and loss on rare tokens falls more than loss overall.
test: A 45-step matched smoke run; then log the mean gate per stage at step 300 and the per-token loss split by token frequency. If gates stay at 0.95 for every token by step 300 the mechanism is inert.
source: own (pretraining version of the open item from https://arxiv.org/html/2510.13876v3)
breaks: A write weight depends on the layer, never on the token.
keeps: Twelve blocks each applied once, the stream mixing, the optimizer split.
kill: Step-45 train loss more than 0.02 nats above the baseline's.

mechanism: Set n_layer to 10 and d_ff to 1300, which keeps non-embedding parameters at 20.9M, below the baseline. At 50M tokens the model is far from converged, and in that regime fewer sequential stages optimize faster per token while the curse of depth says the last blocks contribute least; the Nemotron-Flash depth law was fitted at 100B tokens and does not cover this budget.
prediction: Parameters down 1.7 percent; step time down about 6 percent; train loss 0.01 to 0.03 nats below the baseline through the constant-LR phase, with the gap narrowing in cooldown.
test: 45-step matched runs for 9 blocks at d_ff 1450, 10 at 1300, and the baseline, then a 300-step run of the best; a 14-block arm at d_ff 880 is the control that the direction, not the change itself, matters, and it needs a 3-step memory check first.
source: own (tests the open item from https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18890)

idea: Readout minus the input token (cancel the similarity prior)
mechanism: The script's skip path carries e_t to the output and the head is E, so the direct path's logits are E Eᵀ e_t: a symmetric form that scores tokens similar to the current one, not ones that follow it. At init the self-token logit is about 7.7 against noise of 0.4, and the near-identity Sinkhorn mixing keeps e_t dominant, so every block must first learn to cancel it; the readout becomes mean(streams) minus λ·e_t with a learned scalar λ starting at 1, so the head reads only what the blocks wrote.
prediction: Loss falls faster in the first 100 steps because the branch writes reach the head at full scale after the final norm; no parameter or memory change; step time unchanged. Final loss 0.01 to 0.02 lower if the prior is costly, zero effect if λ is learned to 0.
test: At init, print logit of the current token versus the mean max logit (baseline shows the 7.7 gap, variant shows none); then a 45-step matched smoke run on the same seed.
breaks: The head should read the raw residual including the input embedding; here the input embedding is removed from the readout.
keeps: Tied table, four-stream mean, final RMSNorm, plain cross entropy.
kill: Mean loss over steps 41 to 45 not at least 0.05 below the baseline's at the same steps.

idea: Frequency-split tying (untie only the frequent rows)
mechanism: The brief says the tied matrix ends up output-shaped because output gradients dominate, and that rare rows (loss 11.6 nats at rank 10k+, which equals the unigram cost) only learn frequency, so they are the rows tying protects. Setting "the two sides conflict most where both gradients are large" as an identity means the conflict lives in the frequent rows; add a zero-initialised 4096 x 384 delta that is added to the logits of ids below 4096 in place (GPT-2 merge order is frequency order), leaving all other rows tied.
prediction: Non-embedding params 22.82M (7.4 percent over, inside C3); step time up under 4 percent; loss curve matches the baseline for the first 50 steps then pulls ahead, with the delta rows' cosine to E drifting toward the 0.72 to 0.53 split the paper reports.
test: Build-only parameter count, 3-step timing, then a 45-step matched smoke run; afterwards compare per-token loss for ids below and above 4096.
source: own, builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.26663 and the modded-nanoGPT untie record https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt
breaks: Tying is all-or-nothing across the vocabulary; here the tie is decided per row by frequency.
keeps: Tied lookup for every row, same head, same loss, same optimizer groups (the delta is a 2-D matrix under Muon).
kill: Mean loss over steps 41 to 45 above the baseline's by more than 0.02, or any step slower than 5.0s.

idea: Direction-only tied head with a counted unigram bias
mechanism: The brief's centering paper identifies output anisotropy, and the rare-token loss equals the unigram cost; literalise "row norm equals log frequency" and the consequence is that the tied table spends its norm, which the input lookup also sees, on a quantity a bias can hold. Logits become g·norm(x)·(E/‖E‖_row)ᵀ + b, with b initialised to log counts from one train shard (stored as a parameter so the exam sees it) and g a learned scalar starting at the baseline row norm.
prediction: Step-1 loss near 7.5 instead of 10.8; parameters up by 50,305; no extra logits copy because the bias fuses into the matmul; step time unchanged; rare-token loss falls because their directions are trained without norm pressure.
test: Step-1 loss readout, then a 45-step matched smoke run; falsified if the head start vanishes by step 45.
breaks: A logit is a raw inner product with a shared row whose norm encodes frequency; here the output side sees only direction and frequency lives in a bias.
keeps: Tied directions, stream mean, final norm, cross entropy, optimizer split.
kill: Mean loss over steps 41 to 45 not at least 0.10 below the baseline's.

mechanism: The brief notes residual RMS grows 7.8x through depth and the final RMSNorm sets the softmax temperature to a constant; literalise "RMSNorm equals a temperature of 1/RMS" and the consequence is that per-token magnitude, the sum of how strongly twelve blocks wrote, is a confidence signal thrown away and re-encoded in direction. Scale the normed vector by 1 + α·log(RMS(x_t)/RMS_ref) before the head, α a learned scalar starting at 0.
prediction: Identical to baseline at step 1; per-token RMS spread widens over training as α moves away from 0; no parameter or memory cost since the scale is applied to the 384-wide vector, not the logits.
test: Correlate per-token final RMS with per-token loss on a smoke batch at step 45 (no correlation kills it before training the variant); then a 45-step matched smoke run.
target: residual RMS growth, spread across tokens up
breaks: The final norm should erase per-token magnitude; here magnitude sets the logit temperature.
keeps: Tied head, stream mean, RMSNorm direction, cross entropy.
kill: |α| below 0.01 at step 45, or loss above the baseline's by more than 0.02.

mechanism: Four identical input streams carry no more than one, so 3/4 of the input width is redundant; stream k is initialised with e(x_{t-k}) for k=1..3 (padded with the current token at the window start), giving layer 1 a bigram and trigram for free, which the brief says is what weak early layers under tying miss. The final readout becomes a learned softmax over streams initialised on stream 0 so the head does not see a bag of past tokens.
prediction: 4 readout parameters; activations up 12 MB; step time within 1 percent; loss at steps 10 to 45 clearly below baseline because local context exists before any attention has trained; risk is the uniform block read averaging four tokens' embeddings.
test: 45-step matched smoke run; also inspect read_logits after 45 steps to confirm block 1 shifts toward stream 0.
source: own, inverts the value-embedding re-injection in https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt
breaks: All four streams start as copies of one token's embedding; here they start as a four-token history.
keeps: One tied table, Sinkhorn mixing, block structure, final norm and loss.
kill: Mean loss over steps 41 to 45 not at least 0.05 below the baseline's.

idea: Input-side gradient amplification on the tied table
mechanism: The open item in the brief: output gradients dominate the tied matrix, so multiply the input-side gradient by g with the value-preserving trick (g·e minus (g-1)·e.detach()). AdamW normalises the summed gradient, so scaling one side changes the update direction rather than its size, which is why it is not a no-op.
prediction: No parameter, memory or time change; loss curve diverges from baseline only after a few hundred steps; sweep g in {2, 4, 8}, expecting a gain of 0.005 to 0.01 at g=4 and a loss at g=8.
test: 45-step matched smoke runs at g=4 and g=8 to check neither diverges; the final answer needs the full budget.

mechanism: Inkling normalises the embedding directly after lookup; with a tied table the output pressure inflates frequent rows, so the input scale becomes frequency-dependent and the branch writes are dwarfed for frequent tokens. A 384-gain RMSNorm after lookup fixes the input scale to the write scale regardless of row norm.
prediction: 384 extra parameters; step time unchanged; residual RMS growth through depth drops below 7.8x; small loss gain of 0.003 to 0.006.
test: 45-step matched smoke run and a print of per-layer residual RMS at step 45 against the baseline.

idea: Self-tolerant attention (shifted KV with a learned sink slot)
mechanism: Shared structure: the immune system deletes receptors that bind self during maturation, so that detection capacity is spent on foreign material only; here a token's own key is "self", and under causal attention it always gets a share of the softmax although its content already sits in the residual and the MLP path. Instantiation: after RoPE, shift k, v and kr right by one position along time, drop the last slot, and put a learned sink row (content key, value, rotary key) in slot 0; SDPA stays is_causal, so token t sees the sink and tokens 0..t-1. This inverts assumption 2 in its implicit form
prediction: Parameters +9.6k (12 layers x (384 + 384 + 32)); step time unchanged; loss curve below baseline from the first few hundred steps, since the sink effect appears early; first-token attention mass drops in favor of the sink slot.
test: 45 matched steps against the baseline at the same seed and data order; also a 1-step check that the shifted model's loss at step 1 equals the baseline's within noise, which confirms the shift is not corrupting positions.
target: first-token attention mass, down; loss at late positions, down
breaks: A token's key and value at position t are produced from token t, and every token may attend to itself.
keeps: compress/latent_norm/expand, QK-norm, decoupled RoPE, causal SDPA kernel, all four streams and the Sinkhorn mixing.
kill: mean loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.01 nats above the baseline's at the same seed.

idea: Causal AGC on the latent instead of per-token RMSNorm
mechanism: Shared structure: a radio receiver's automatic gain control divides the signal by a slow running envelope, so the absolute level is bounded but the modulation survives; dividing each sample by its own magnitude would destroy the message. The latent RMSNorm is exactly per-sample normalization, and the value vectors are the modulation: every token's value leaves expand with the same RMS, so a filler token and a rare content token are equally loud. Instantiation: divide the latent by the square root of the causal running mean of its mean-square over positions 0..t (a cumsum divided by t+1, with t
prediction: Parameters unchanged; step time +1% (one cumsum per layer); value-norm spread across tokens becomes wide and bimodal within the first 100 steps; rare-token loss falls more than frequent-token loss; nothing else changes at step 1.
test: 45 matched steps; plus a histogram of per-token value norms at step 45 to confirm the spread actually opened (if it stays near uniform the mechanism is inert and the idea is dead regardless of loss).
breaks: Every token's latent has unit RMS when it enters the expansion.
keeps: compress and expand shapes, the learned norm weight, k_norm and q_norm, RoPE, SDPA, the block structure.
kill: mean loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.01 nats above baseline, or any step in the first 45 more than 0.5 nats above the baseline's matched step (early-envelope instability).

mechanism: Shared structure: in hedonic markets a buyer's utility for a good is a match term between the buyer's needs and the good's attributes plus a price term that is independent of the buyer; attention has the match term (query times key) but this recipe has removed the price term, because q_norm and k_norm make the content logit a bounded cosine, RoPE rotates away any constant in the rotary part, and bias=False everywhere means q cannot hold a constant component unless the model sacrifices a residual dimension to a massive activation (which is exactly how sinks form in practice). Instantiation: app
prediction: Parameters +9.3k; step time within +3% if SDPA keeps its fused kernel at head dim 104; max attention logit grows beyond the cosine bound within the first 200 steps; first-token attention mass falls because salience no longer needs a massive activation.
test: 3-step timing first (a fallback to the math kernel shows as >1.3x step time and must be fixed by repadding before any loss check); then 45 matched steps.
target: max attention logit, up; first-token attention mass, down
breaks: The attention logit is a bounded bilinear match between a normalized query and a normalized key with no query-independent term.
keeps: QK-norm on the content dims, decoupled RoPE, SDPA, the latent compression, wo, the block.
kill: mean loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.01 nats above baseline, or step time above 1.3x baseline at the 3-step timing.

mechanism: Shared structure, from observer design in control: the measurement y = Cx can be low-dimensional, since it only has to locate the state, while the state that is propagated must be carried in full. Keys are the measurement (which past token), values are the state (what gets transported through wo into the residual). The baseline compresses both through one 128-dim normed latent, so a layer can move at most 128 independent dims of past content per token no matter how many heads read it: six heads reading 64 dims each are forced to copy correlated content. Instantiation: keys from a 64-dim normed
prediction: Parameters +49k per layer, +0.59M total (under the +2.12M cap); step time +2%; loss at late positions and on recall tokens falls more than overall loss; if instead the 64-dim key latent hurts at step 45, the fallback keeps the 128 key latent and still fits (+1.77M).
test: parameter count from --build-only; 45 matched steps; a 3-step timing.
target: recall-token loss, down; loss at late positions, down
breaks: Keys and values share one low-rank latent, so the per-token transport bandwidth of a layer equals the latent rank.
keeps: wq, QK-norm, decoupled RoPE, wo, the six heads, the block and streams.
kill: mean loss over steps 41-45 more than 0.01 nats above baseline for both the 64-dim and the 128-dim key-latent variants.

idea: Companding eps on the latent norm
mechanism: Raising latent_norm's eps from 1e-6 to the scale of the latent's own mean-square turns the hard per-token normalization into mu-law style companding: tokens with weak latents are attenuated instead of amplified to unit RMS, strong ones saturate. The latent mean-square at init is about 0.15 (weights of std 0.02 on unit-RMS input, 384 fan-in), so eps near 0.1 is the soft regime; this inverts assumption 4 cheaply, and keys are unaffected because k_norm cancels the gain, so the test isolates value scale.
prediction: Parameters and step time unchanged; loss curve identical for the first 50 steps and diverging later as the latent scale grows under Muon; rare-token loss moves first.
test: 45-step smoke at eps in {0.01, 0.1, 1.0} against baseline; sweep range 1e-2 to 1e0 on a log grid; since Muon grows the latent scale over training, also log the latent mean-square at step 45 to see where eps sits relative to it.

idea: Per-head low-rank residual on the shared latent (LRKV on top of MLA)
mechanism: Keep the shared normed 128-dim latent for keys and values, and add for each head a rank-16 private path from x (384-to-16-to-64) for its key and for its value, so heads can diverge from the common subspace. This inverts assumption 1 (a 128-dim latent is wide enough for six heads), and tests the open item of LRKV's shared-plus-residual design on a normed latent at 21M.
prediction: Parameters +86k per layer, +1.03M total; step time +3%; attention entropy in deep layers becomes less uniform across heads (more specialized heads); loss lower from mid-training on.
test: parameter count; 45 matched steps; per-head key-subspace cosine at step 45 to confirm heads actually diverged.
target: attention entropy in deep layers, down (more peaked heads)

idea: Short causal conv on the latent before expansion
mechanism: A depthwise causal conv of kernel 4 over time on the 128-dim latent, applied before the norm and expansion, makes each key and value describe a 4-token local context instead of one token, which lets the attention head match on short phrases and frees the softmax from spending heads on adjacent-token lookups. It inverts assumption 3 (compression is worth paying for only as a cache) by using the narrow latent as the cheap place for temporal mixing: the conv costs 128x4 parameters per layer there versus 768x4 after expansion.
prediction: Parameters +512 per layer; step time +2%; loss curve lower early (local n-gram structure is learned fastest) with the gap narrowing but persisting.
test: 45 matched steps; a 3-step timing; kernel 2 versus 4 as the one knob.

idea: Spectrum re-derived from the context, theta 10000 to 480
mechanism: With theta 10000 and 16 rotary pairs, pair i has wavelength 2π·10000^(i/16): pairs 9 to 15 never complete a turn in 1024 tokens and pairs 12 to 15 rotate under 1.0 rad end to end, so 8 of the 32 positional dims are a constant vector, i.e. an un-normed 8-dim content key shared across heads that duplicates the 64 content dims. Setting the lowest wavelength to 2048 gives theta = (2048/2π)^(16/15) ≈ 480, so all 16 pairs span wavelengths 6 to 2048 log-spaced and the 64 to 2048 band, where the current spectrum has only 3 pairs, gets 7; a learned log-frequency per pair initialized at this spectrum is
prediction: Parameters unchanged (or +16 per layer if frequencies are learned), step time unchanged, loss at positions 256 to 1024 lower by 0.01 to 0.02 nats, early loss curve ahead of baseline from the first 100 steps because mid-range offsets become resolvable.
test: 45-step matched smoke runs at theta in {200, 480, 2000, 10000}, same seed and data order; then one 50M run at theta 480 if the curve separates. Position-bucketed loss on the self-report split shows where the gain lands.
source: own; the diagnosis extends https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10134 (LeRoPE's high-norm positional band)
breaks: The rotary base is a constant that scales up with context and never needs to be scaled down when the context is 1024.
keeps: Decoupled 32-dim rotary key, QK-norm, head count, SDPA scale, same apply_rope.
kill: Mean loss over steps 40 to 45 at theta 480 above the baseline's by 0.02 or more, or every theta in the sweep within noise of each other (then frequencies do not matter at this budget).

idea: Decay-proof temperature: per-head log-scale with unit fixed point
mechanism: After RMSNorm the content logit has std 0.82·g_q·g_k and the measured max logit 22.7 needs g_q·g_k ≈ 3.5, so the deep layers grew their gains to about 1.9 each while AdamW with weight decay 0.1 pulls every gain toward 0, i.e. toward uniform attention, at 3e-4 per step for 1525 steps. Replace the gains by exp(γ) per dim so decay returns them to the derived value 1, and add one per-head log-temperature τ_h in the SDPA scale, exp(τ_h)/sqrt(96), soft-clipped to [−1, 2], so sharpening is a 6-parameter decision per layer that the regularizer does not fight.
prediction: Parameters change by +72; step time unchanged; max attention logit in layers 8 to 12 exceeds the baseline's by step 300 and deep-layer entropy drops earlier; final loss 0.005 to 0.015 lower. If the gain was never regularizer-limited, τ stays near 0 and the curves coincide.
test: Dump q_norm and k_norm gain norms per layer from the baseline checkpoint: if the sharp layers sit near 1.9 and the others near 1.0, the decay is binding. Then 45-step matched smoke; then 3 seeds.
source: own; the learnable-g idea is in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.04245, the clipping warning in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.12956
target: max attention logit, up in deep layers; attention entropy in deep layers, down earlier
breaks: Attention temperature is a side effect of 128 per-dim gains whose weight-decay fixed point is uniform attention.
keeps: QK RMSNorm, 1/sqrt(96) as the unit scale, AdamW grouping and decay untouched (the reparametrization moves the fixed point, not the optimizer).
kill: Baseline gain norms within 1.15 of 1.0 in every layer (decay was not binding), or 45-step loss above baseline by 0.02.

idea: Re-entangle: RoPE on 16 content dims, delete the decoupled key
mechanism: Decoupled RoPE exists so the latent can be absorbed into the query at inference with a cache; this script never runs with a cache, so the 32 rotary q dims per head plus the shared rotary projection are a cost paid for nothing. Remove Attention.rotary and the rotary slice of wq, apply RoPE to 16 of the 64 content dims of q and k after q_norm and k_norm (rotation preserves the norm, so QK-norm still holds), with the theta-480 spectrum over 8 pairs; positional keys become per-head and content-dependent through the latent.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters fall by 86,016 per layer, 1.03M total; SDPA head dim 96 to 64 cuts attention-score compute by a third, about 3 percent of the step; loss equal to or 0.005 below baseline, which counts because fewer parameters are always allowed.
test: Parameter count by --build-only (20.21M expected); 3-step timing; 45-step matched smoke; the partial-RoPE paper's finding that 10 percent of dims suffice says 25 percent should not hurt.
source: own; builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11611 and the open item in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.11486
target: validation loss only, with step time down
breaks: Position and content must live in disjoint channels because MLA's inference-time absorption requires it.
keeps: Latent KV compression, QK-norm, 6 heads of 64, output projection, causal SDPA.
kill: 45-step loss above baseline by 0.03, which would mean the full-rank x-to-rotary path, not the decoupling, is what the keys needed.

idea: Offset-aware values: rotate values by j, un-rotate output by i
mechanism: Attention output is position-blind: a head that retrieves a token cannot tell the MLP whether it came from 1 or 500 positions back, so distance must be re-derived by another head. Apply RoPE to 16 of the 64 value dims with the longest 8 wavelengths (32 to 2048) and apply the inverse rotation at the query position to the SDPA output, so y_i = Σ a_ij R(j−i) v_j and the output carries the attended offset in phase.
prediction: Zero parameters, two extra (B,H,T,16) rotations per layer, under 1 percent step time; recall-token loss and loss at late positions lower by 0.01; early curve unchanged for the first 100 steps because the phase channel starts unused.
test: 3-step timing, 45-step matched smoke, then one full run with the position-bucketed self-report. A synthetic check: train 200 steps and probe whether a linear read of the 16 value dims predicts the attended offset.
target: recall-token loss, down; loss at late positions, down
scope: validation loss at 1024, and more at long context
breaks: Values carry no positional information and the attention output is a position-free mixture.
keeps: Keys and queries as they are, softmax, causal mask, same frequencies, un-rotated 48 value dims.
kill: 45-step loss above baseline by 0.02, or the offset probe at 200 steps no better than chance.

idea: No self-key: drop the diagonal and make the no-op an explicit null key
mechanism: First-token mass is under 0.6 percent, so the no-op in this recipe is most likely the self position: a head that wants to do nothing attends to its own value, which the residual already carries, and the self logit inflates the softmax denominator and cools attention over real context. Mask the diagonal and prepend one learned null key per head with a zero value, so doing nothing is a single logit that is position- and content-free and every unit of context mass is real retrieval.
prediction: Parameters +6×96 per layer; attn_mask path instead of is_causal costs up to 30 percent on attention, about 3 to 5 percent of the step; deep-layer entropy over real keys drops, attention mass to the null key tracks what diagonal mass used to be, loss 0.005 to 0.01 lower.
test: Free first: measure diagonal attention mass per layer on the baseline checkpoint. Then 3-step timing and a 45-step matched smoke.
source: own; the sink half contrasts with the negative result in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.13392 and MiMo's positive one in https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780v1
target: attention entropy in deep layers, down over real keys; first-token attention mass, unchanged
breaks: Every token's own key is in its attention set and serves as the free no-op.
keeps: Causal ordering, softmax, head count, QK-norm, decoupled RoPE.
kill: Baseline diagonal mass below 5 percent in layers 8 to 12 (there is no self no-op to remove), or 45-step loss above baseline by 0.03.

idea: Post-SDPA sigmoid output gate per head
mechanism: A query-dependent sigmoid gate on the attention output adds nonlinearity after the softmax mixture and gives heads a content-based way to zero their contribution, which the Qwen study found removes sinks and massive activations; at 21M it also lets the deep layers reach entropy 0.67 only on the heads that need it. Gate from x with a 384-to-384 projection, elementwise, before wo.
prediction: Parameters +147,456 per layer, +1.77M total, 8.3 percent and under the 10 percent cap; step time +2 to 3 percent; residual RMS growth and max attention logit lower; loss 0.005 to 0.01 lower.
test: --build-only count (23.01M expected), 3-step timing, 45-step matched smoke; the cheap control is a per-head gate of 384-to-6 (+2,304 per layer) to see whether the elementwise form is where the gain is.
target: residual RMS growth, down; max attention logit, down

idea: Per-head rotary keys instead of one shared key
mechanism: One 32-dim rotary key for 6 heads was chosen for 128-head DeepSeek, where sharing is cheap; here each head's positional selectivity comes only from its own qr against a key all heads share, so content-gated positional patterns differ per head only through the query. Widen Attention.rotary from 32 to 6×32 and drop the expand in the concat.
prediction: Parameters +61,440 per layer, +0.74M total; step time unchanged; loss 0.003 to 0.008 lower, larger if heads specialize to different offsets.
test: Sweep rotary key heads in {1, 2, 6} on 45-step matched smoke runs; count by --build-only.

mechanism: For heads 3 to 5, the key at position j is the (post-RoPE) key of token j−1 while the value stays token j's; a query that matches "the token before me last time" directly reads "what followed it". Today this needs two layers (a previous-token head feeding an induction head); fusing it frees those layers for other circuits and should lower loss on repeated spans within 1024 tokens.
prediction: Zero parameter change, step time within 1%; training loss separates from baseline after the induction bump (roughly step 150 to 300), gap of 0.02 to 0.04 nats at 50M tokens, largest on late positions.
test: 45-step matched smoke run on seed 0; 3-step timing; unit check that query i never sees token i+1 (compare logits for a sequence truncated at i).
target: recall-token loss, down; loss at late positions, down
breaks: The key a query scores and the value it reads belong to the same token.
keeps: softmax causal attention, the latent KV path, QK-norm, RoPE on the rotary slice, the same wo and head count.
kill: mean loss over steps 40 to 45 more than 0.02 nats above the baseline's at the same steps.

mechanism: Drop the V half of expand and the shared wo; each head aggregates the 128-d normalized latent directly as its value and writes it through its own 384×128 map. Today each head's value-to-output path is wo_h·E_v,h, rank 64 even though the latent has 128 dims; the cap is paid for nothing because at 6 heads the concatenation never uses the extra rank. DeepSeek-style absorption makes this free at inference; here it is applied at training time to raise per-head rank.
prediction: Non-embedding params 22.42M (+1.18M, under the 23.37M cap); SDPA value width 128 so step time +3 to 6%; loss gap of 0.01 to 0.02 nats at the end, visible from the start since it is capacity, not a circuit.
test: --build-only parameter count; 3-step timing and peak VRAM (fails if memory-efficient kernel is forced and VRAM passes 5.6 GB); 45-step matched smoke run.
source: own, builds on the MLA absorption in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.04434
breaks: Each head writes a 64-d value and heads combine by concatenation into one 384×384 map.
keeps: the 128-d latent, latent_norm, 6 query heads of 64+32, softmax causal attention, the same K path.
kill: step-45 loss not below baseline by at least 0.005 nats, or step time above 5.3 s.

idea: Re-query hop (two retrievals per layer, shared K/V)
mechanism: After the first SDPA, feed the concatenated head output y through the existing wq and q_norm to form a second query and attend once more to the same K and V, then apply wo to the second result (first result added as a skip). A composition like "find the entity, then find what it did" takes two layers today; with shared K/V the second hop costs no parameters and lets 12 layers act like 24 hops for retrieval.
prediction: Zero new parameters; step time +12 to 18% (one extra SDPA and one extra wq matmul); loss gap 0.015 to 0.03 nats, appearing after step 200.
test: 3-step timing (kill above 6.0 s); 45-step matched smoke run; ablation with the second hop's wo input zeroed to confirm the gain is from the hop.
breaks: A layer retrieves once: one hop, then the result enters the stream.
keeps: K/V, wq, wo, head layout and the residual write are unchanged; the second hop reuses existing tensors.
kill: step-45 loss more than 0.01 nats above baseline, or step time above 6.0 s.

idea: Two-depth keys (queries see the previous layer's K/V too)
mechanism: Each layer concatenates its own K and V with the previous layer's K and V along the key axis and runs one softmax over 2T keys with a causal mask repeated twice. The query chooses depth as well as position, so a feature the stream overwrote between layers is still retrievable, and attention patterns can specialise by depth without doubling layers.
prediction: Zero new parameters; attention score and value compute doubles, roughly +10% forward, but the explicit mask forces the memory-efficient kernel, so step time +20 to 30%; memory is the risk at 0.1 GB headroom.
test: 3-step timing and peak VRAM first (kill on VRAM above 5.6 GB); then 45-step matched smoke run; ablation where the previous layer's keys are masked out must recover baseline exactly.
source: own, related to cross-layer KV sharing in https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02770 and value residuals in https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17897v4
target: attention entropy in deep layers, up; recall-token loss, down
breaks: A layer's keys and values come only from that layer's own latent.
keeps: the compress/expand path per layer, one softmax per head, wo, head count, causal order.
kill: step-45 loss not below baseline by 0.005 nats, or VRAM above 5.6 GB, or step time above 6.5 s.

mechanism: Prepend a learned 96-d key per head and a zero value, plus a dummy zero query row so is_causal still aligns; every query can dump mass on the sink instead of on token 0. MiMo's ablation shows a measurable gain, and this architecture has no sink mechanism yet, so the first-token attention mass is wasted on an arbitrary token.
prediction: +576 parameters per layer; step time unchanged (flash kernel kept, T+1 keys); first-token attention mass falls sharply; loss gain 0.005 to 0.012 nats, mostly in the first half of training.
test: 45-step matched smoke run; measure first-token attention mass on a fixed batch at step 45 with a manual softmax, baseline versus sink.
target: first-token attention mass, down; max attention logit, down

mechanism: Multiply each head's SDPA output by sigmoid(x_norm[:, :, :32]·W_h) before wo, where x_norm is the attention input already in Attention.forward; the gate makes the head's write conditional on the token so a head can abstain instead of writing noise. This is the open test the brief asks for: whether the Qwen gate interacts with QK-norm and four-stream mixing, and whether it flattens the 10x layer-0 attention gradient.
prediction: +192 parameters per layer; step time +1%; gradient norm spread across layers shrinks; loss gain 0.005 to 0.01 nats.
test: 45-step matched smoke run; log per-layer attention gradient norms at step 45 and compare the layer-0 to median ratio.

mechanism: Set n_head=3 so each head's content key is 128-d, matching the latent width; today a 64-d head key is a rank-64 slice of a 128-d latent, and the Pythia ablation says the penalty from small QK dims is the one head-size effect that is not neutral. Fewer heads also cut SDPA and wq cost.
prediction: Non-embedding params −442k; step time −3 to −5%; loss within ±0.01 nats of baseline, with the 12×32 arm clearly worse.
test: Sweep n_head over {3, 6, 12} with 45-step matched smoke runs and --build-only counts; keep 3 only if it is not worse than 6 at step 45 and the timing gain is real.

idea: Slow automatic gain control on the MLP write
mechanism: Shared structure: a radio receiver chain has amplifier stages whose output envelope is measured over a window far longer than the signal, and a feedback gain keeps each stage inside the next stage's linear range; our chain is 12 blocks writing into a shared stream, the "signal" is the token-to-token variation of a write, the "envelope" is the batch-level RMS, and the stuck measurement is an MLP write RMS that drifts to 10.9 because magnitude can only be set by inflating three Muon-trained matrices against weight decay. Instantiation: the MLP keeps a detached running RMS of its own output (mome

idea: Divisive normalization pools in the hidden layer
mechanism: Shared structure: in visual cortex a neuron's drive is divided by the pooled energy of its neighbours plus a semi-saturation constant, which decorrelates responses and enforces a soft winner-take-all; ecology says the same thing as competitive exclusion, overlapping niches cannot coexist once resources are contested; our 1077 hidden units all read the same token vector with no lateral interaction, so nothing stops many units from learning the same feature. Instantiation: with the hidden size at 1072 (67 pools of 16, fewer parameters), the gated product p is replaced by p divided by the square
prediction: mean pairwise correlation of hidden units within a layer falls; hidden RMS per unit stays below 1 by construction so the write-RMS growth has to go through the down projection alone; parameters −5,760; step time +2 to 4%; memory +0 (the pool statistics are tiny).

mechanism: Shared structure: the immune repertoire stays filled by homeostatic proliferation, a clone whose niche is empty receives unopposed survival cytokine and expands, so no antigen class goes unwatched; our hidden units are clones, the gate pre-activation is the activation threshold, and the unopposed signal is low usage; DeepSeek's aux-loss-free expert balancing is the same rule applied to experts, and nobody applies it to dense hidden units even though their usage is extremely skewed at small scale. source: own (import; the balancing rule is from https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19348v1 and the V3 aux-loss-free routing)

idea: Three activation populations in one hidden layer
mechanism: Ecology's functional-diversity result says a community with complementary resource use is more productive than a monoculture of the single best species; the hidden layer is a monoculture of SiLU-gated units even though ReLU²-gated units (sparse, high-order) and plain bilinear units (smooth quadratic) tie or beat it in different regimes. Split the 1077 units into thirds: SiLU-gated, ReLU²-gated and bilinear with no activation, same three matrices, so the layer can route each feature to the nonlinearity that fits it.
prediction: parameters, memory and step time within 1% of the baseline; the down-projection column norms of the three populations stay within 2x of each other if all three are used; loss curve equal or slightly below the baseline from step 100 on.
test: 45 matched steps; at step 45 read the three populations' column norms; a population below 30% of the others is dead weight and the idea fails.
breaks: all hidden units in a layer share one activation function.
keeps: gated form, widths, init, optimizers.
kill: mean loss over steps 40 to 45 more than 0.02 nats above the baseline's.

mechanism: Keep the total feed-forward parameter count fixed but make the hidden size grow linearly from about 700 in layer 0 to about 1454 in layer 11 (mean 1077), so early layers that mostly do local lexical work are cheap and late layers that compose features get the capacity. The brief lists this open at 21M; the four-stream residual makes late layers see a richer read-out, which strengthens the case for putting width late.
prediction: parameters equal to the baseline (verified by build-only), total hidden activation memory equal, step time within 2%; loss 0.005 to 0.015 lower at 50M tokens. A stackable tune: raise the mean to 1150 using 0.9M of the parameter headroom if a 3-step smoke keeps peak VRAM under 5.6 GB.

idea: Token-shifted value path in the gate
mechanism: The up projection reads a per-channel learned blend of the current and previous token's normalized input (blend weight initialized to 1, so the start is the baseline) while the gate reads the current token only, so the MLP can form bigram features directly instead of spending attention heads on previous-token copying. Pretraining ablations of this inside a gated MLP are missing per the brief; RWKV uses it as a standing component.
prediction: parameters +384 per layer; memory +3 MB per layer; step time within 2%; the blend weights drift below 0.9 in early layers if the path is used; first-token attention mass drops as previous-token heads are freed.
test: 45 matched steps plus the blend-weight values at step 45; a 3-step timing.
target: first-token attention mass, down; validation loss, down.

idea: Peri-LN output norm on the MLP branch
mechanism: Apply an RMSNorm with a learned per-channel scale to the MLP output before it is written, with the scale initialized small (about 0.1) so early writes stay modest. This is the instantaneous, per-token counterpart of the slow gain above: if this wins and the slow gain does not, per-token limiting matters; if the reverse, the batch-level gain was the point.
prediction: per-token write RMS is fixed by the learned scale; parameters +384 per layer; memory +3 MB per layer; step time within 2%; gradient norm spread across depth narrows.
test: 45 matched steps against both the baseline and the slow-gain run; discard if loss is 0.02 above the baseline at step 45.
target: residual RMS growth, down; gradient norm spread, down.

idea: Subtract the streams, add a thirteenth layer
mechanism: Collapse the residual to one stream with mixing at identity and no write gains, which by the audit changes nothing the head can see, and spend the freed 0.3 GB and the 1.83M parameter headroom on a 13th block. Depth is the one axis the measurements say is under-provisioned, and the frontier recipes keep the stream machinery only because it is cheap behind fused kernels, which this card lacks.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters rise to about 23.07M, under the 23.37M cap. Step time rises by at most 8 percent from the extra block minus the stream overhead, so under 5.2 s. Peak memory stays under 5.6 GB. Validation loss falls by 0.01 to 0.02 nats, the usual gain of one extra layer at this depth.
test: Build-only for the parameter count, a 3-step timing and peak memory check, then 45 matched steps against the baseline on one seed.
breaks: The residual must be four streams mixed by a doubly stochastic matrix; here it is one stream and the budget goes to depth.
keeps: Every block, norm, attention and MLP is unchanged, as is the tied head and the optimizer split.
kill: Loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 above the same-seed baseline by more than 0.02 nats, or peak memory above 5.6 GB.

mechanism: Reinterpret the stream axis as depth lag: each sublayer reads a signed combination of the current residual and the residuals one, two and three stages earlier, with weights initialized to read only the current one, and writes its branch into the single live residual. Differences between lagged residuals are exactly the last few branch outputs, so a block can add or subtract its recent predecessors per stage, the depth-local version of Attention Residuals and MUDD with zero Sinkhorn and the subtractive mixing the brief says the Birkhoff constraint forbids.
prediction: Parameter count falls by about 1,300. Step time drops below the baseline because no 4x4 mix and no fourfold residual traffic remain. Peak memory falls by about 0.2 GB since the lagged residuals are already saved for backward. Loss curve matches the baseline for the first 20 steps and then runs below
test: 3-step timing and memory, then 45 matched steps on one seed; also log the signed read weights of the final checkpoint to confirm they leave the one-hot init.
target: residual RMS growth, down, and gradient norm spread, down
breaks: Streams are copies of the same state mixed by a static non-negative matrix; here streams are the same residual at different depths read with signed weights.
keeps: One additive residual carries the signal to the head; attention, MLP and norms are untouched.
kill: Loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 above the same-seed baseline by more than 0.03 nats, or any NaN.

mechanism: Keep four streams but make them different by construction: each stream is an exponential moving average over depth of the branch outputs with a fixed decay per stream, one at 1, the others at 0.9, 0.7 and 0.5, and each sublayer and the head read a signed combination initialized to the undecayed stream. Decayed streams have bounded norm and hold a recent-layers view at fixed scale, which gives later blocks a clean signal that the 7.8x-grown main residual buries.
prediction: Parameters unchanged within a few hundred. Step time at or below the baseline since the mix is a diagonal scale. Memory equal to the baseline. Residual RMS on the decayed streams stays within 2x of a single branch output through all 12 layers, and the loss runs below the baseline from mid-training o

breaks: The mixing must be doubly stochastic and norm preserving; here it is a contraction with row sums below 1.
keeps: The undecayed stream is exactly the baseline residual, so the model can recover the baseline by leaving the reads at init.
kill: Loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 above the same-seed baseline by more than 0.03 nats.

mechanism: Attention writes its output into streams 0 and 1 only and the MLP into streams 2 and 3 only, with the mix at identity and signed reads per sublayer initialized uniform. Attention history and MLP history then live in separate streams instead of superposed in one 384-wide residual, so each consumer can choose how much of the other writer's history it reads, which the identical writes of the current design make impossible.
prediction: Parameters unchanged within a few hundred. Step time below the baseline. Memory equal to the baseline. Attention-stream RMS grows slower than the MLP-stream RMS, and the read weights of the attention sublayer tilt toward the attention streams within the first thousand steps.
test: 45 matched steps on one seed with per-stream RMS logging, and a check that the head still receives both histories.
target: residual RMS growth, down, and recall-token loss, down
breaks: Every sublayer writes to every stream; here each stream has exactly one kind of writer.
keeps: The head reads the mean of all streams, so the full residual sum reaches the output as before.
kill: Loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 above the same-seed baseline by more than 0.03 nats.

mechanism: Replace the static write gains with per-token gains from a linear map of the normalized branch output to four logits, so each token decides which streams its branch output enters. Dynamic writes create the stream diversity the static design never builds, which the HC paper showed beats static mixing at expansion four.
prediction: Parameters rise by about 37K. Step time rises by at most 2 percent. Measured stream divergence, the RMS of differences between streams over the mean stream RMS, rises from about 1 percent to over 20 percent by the end of training. Loss gain is small, under 0.01 nats.
test: 3-step timing, then 45 matched steps on one seed with the divergence statistic logged.

idea: Orthogonal Cayley mixing in place of Sinkhorn
mechanism: Parameterize each 4x4 mix as the Cayley transform of a learned skew-symmetric matrix, six parameters, which is exactly orthogonal, allows negative entries and starts at exact identity. This removes the 20 iterations and their accumulated approximation error and permits subtractive mixing.
prediction: Parameters fall by about 500. Step time falls by 2 to 4 percent. Loss matches the baseline unless the mix leaves identity, which is measured by its Frobenius distance from identity at the end of training.
test: 3-step timing, then 45 matched steps, then a full run inspected for the distance from identity per block.

mechanism: Raise the diagonal write logits from 0.03 to a larger value a and set the off-diagonal ones to minus a, so attention writes mostly to stream 0 and the MLP mostly to stream 1 from the first step while streams 2 and 3 stay close to the embedding. One constant turns the dead copies into an attention stream, an MLP stream and two embedding skips.

test: Sweep a over 1, 2 and 4 with 45 matched steps each on one seed, comparing the step 41 to 45 average.

mechanism: Normalize each of the 4 streams separately before the softmax read, with a gain of shape 4 by 384 whose init is 1.5 on stream s's own channel quarter and 0.83 elsewhere, so gains average to 1 and the read-out at init equals the baseline. This inverts assumption 2, norm on the collapsed read-out. Today the loudest stream dominates every read regardless of read logits, and the identical-copy streams only diverge through the 0.03 write asymmetry. Per-stream norm decouples which stream is read from which stream is loud, and the partitioned gains give the write and mix logits stream-specific gradie

mechanism: In the per-block init loop, set write logits so layer l writes at weight 1 into stream l mod 4 and at weight 0.005 into the others, instead of weight 1 into all four. This inverts assumption 4, scaled init under mixing weights, and assumption 5, structurally identical layers. Each stream then holds the embedding plus six sublayer writes instead of twenty-four, so a deep layer's write is a four-times larger fraction of its lane, which is the curse-of-depth relief that LayerNorm Scaling buys with a fixed multiplier. A uniform read still sees the embedding plus a quarter of every write, so the fu

keeps: Sinkhorn mixing, uniform read init, the head's mean over streams, the 1/sqrt(2L) branch init, which Muon erases anyway.

mechanism: Each read-out and the final norm divide by sqrt of half the token's own mean square plus half the causal running mean square of the prefix, instead of the token's own mean square alone. This inverts assumption 1 in its hidden form: that the norm must erase every token's magnitude. Position 0 is unchanged. A token that has received more writes than its context average keeps up to sqrt 2 of that signal and a quiet token stays quiet, so the stream's per-token magnitude becomes a readable feature for the MLP and value paths, which per-token RMSNorm destroys. The bound keeps every read within a fac
