keeps: Pre-norm placement, learned per-channel gains, collapsed read-out, all attention and MLP shapes.
kill: Any NaN, or loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 higher than the matched baseline's by more than 0.02 nats.

mechanism: The final norm multiplies its unit-RMS output by exp(a plus b times log RMS of the pre-norm mean stream), two scalars under Adam, both starting at 0 so the model is the baseline at init. This inverts assumption 1's output side: the head gets a confidence channel from how much the stack wrote to a token, instead of expressing confidence only through direction alignment with tied embedding rows. The multiply is applied to the 384-wide vector, so there is no extra logit tensor and no memory cost.
prediction: Two parameters added, no step-time change. Identical loss for the first 10 steps, then a small improvement concentrated on high-frequency tokens where sharper distributions pay. b moves away from 0 within 45 steps if the channel is useful.
test: A 45-step matched-seed run logging a and b every 5 steps. Build-only count confirms plus 2.
target: loss on rare tokens: down, with calibration improving where the stream is quiet
breaks: The head's logit scale is independent of the residual stream's magnitude.
keeps: Tied head, RMSNorm direction normalization, every block unchanged.
kill: Absolute b under 0.02 at step 45 while loss is not below the baseline's, or loss averaged over steps 41 to 45 higher by more than 0.01 nats.

idea: Branch output norm with Muon-aware gain
mechanism: Add an RMSNorm on each attention and MLP output before the write, as in Peri-LN and Gemma 4's pre-plus-post placement, and drop the 1/sqrt(2L) branch init. This inverts assumption 1, pre-norm only, and assumption 4. The recipe-specific reason: Muon grows every branch matrix at the same per-step spectral rate, so write magnitude drifts upward uniformly and the scaled init is erased in 50 steps, whereas an Adam-owned gain on the branch output holds the write scale as a learned per-channel quantity. Gain init is 0.2, paired with the embedding at std 1 and the final gain at 0.05 from the next sket
prediction: Parameters rise by 9,216. Step time rises under 2 percent. Gradient norm spread across depth narrows and the residual RMS at block 11 grows less than 1.5 times over training.
test: A 3-step timing. A 45-step matched-seed run with the global gradient norm and block-11 stream RMS logged every 15 steps.
target: residual RMS growth: flat across training; gradient norm spread: down

idea: Unit-scale embedding, temperature in the final gain
mechanism: Initialize the tied embedding at std 1.0 instead of 0.02 and the final norm gain at 0.05 instead of 1, so initial logits keep std near 1. This inverts assumption 3, uniform std 0.02 regardless of role. The embedding is under Adam at lr 3e-3 and moves slowly, while branch writes grow under Muon, so by mid-training the token identity is a few percent of the stream for every layer past 0. At std 1 the identity signal stays comparable to the writes throughout the budget, which is what Inkling's embedding norm and the speedrun's large embedding learning rate also buy.
prediction: No parameter or step-time change. Initial loss within 0.2 of the baseline's. Faster descent in the first 200 steps and lower loss on rare tokens, whose identity otherwise fades deepest in the stack.
test: Sweep embedding std over 0.3 and 1.0 and final gain init over 0.02, 0.05 and 0.1 in 45-step matched-seed runs. Check the first-step loss is under 11.5.

mechanism: Initialize the MLP-side pre-norm gain of block l at (l plus 1) to the power minus alpha, leaving attention gains at 1 because QK-norm makes the attention path scale-free apart from values. This tests the brief's open item on LayerNorm Scaling under mixing weights. In this recipe the scaling collapses to a gain init: the gain is learned, so a fixed multiplier is only a starting point, and the paper's bad interaction with scaled init is moot since Muon erases that init. Deep MLPs then write less at the start, so depth-wise variance growth slows and the gain learns the right level under Adam.
prediction: No parameter or step-time change. Residual RMS at block 11 lower at step 45. Loss within 0.01 of the baseline early and slightly below it late.
test: Sweep alpha over 0.25 and 0.5 and apply to MLP gains only versus both gains, in 45-step matched-seed runs with block-11 stream RMS logged.

idea: Embedding stream and write-disjoint streams (limit: stream count to one)
mechanism: Push the stream count to one and the baseline does not change at init: the doubly stochastic mixing preserves the stream sum, the read softmax starts uniform, and the write weights are 1.015 versus 0.995, so all four streams are copies of one residual and the head's mean is exactly a plain residual. The fix the limit suggests is to make the streams carry different things by construction: stream 0 is never written (it stays the token embedding, a free U-Net skip to every block), stream 1 receives only attention writes, stream 2 only MLP writes, stream 3 receives everything; reads start uniform
prediction: Zero parameter and memory change, step time unchanged; the between-stream deviation RMS over mean RMS rises from near zero to above 0.5 by step 200; validation loss down 0.01 to 0.02 with the gain concentrated on rare tokens, which live in the embedding stream.
test: First, a 200-step baseline smoke that prints deviation-over-mean RMS per block; if it is already above 0.3 the limit argument is wrong and the idea dies before any training. Then a 45-step matched smoke against baseline, then 3 seeds.
breaks: Every branch writes to every stream with near-equal weight, so the streams are interchangeable copies.
keeps: Four streams, Sinkhorn mixing, softmax reads, the head's mean, all block weights and the optimizer.
kill: Train loss at step 45 more than 0.03 nats above the baseline's step-45 loss, or stream deviation still under 0.1 at step 200.

idea: Looped middle six with per-pass routing
mechanism: The exam fixes tokens, not compute, and the baseline leaves half its time budget unused; apply blocks 3 to 8 a second time after block 11 is reached in the first pass is wrong, so instead run the stack as 0-2, 3-8, 3-8, 9-11 with the second pass owning its own read, write, mix logits and RMSNorm weights. The routing logits are the per-loop adapter: the same weights act on a differently composed stream state, which is the cheapest form of the LoRA that Relaxed Recursive Transformers needed.
prediction: Parameters up by about 6,000; step time 1.35x to 1.45x with the second pass checkpointed; peak VRAM at or below baseline because six blocks are recomputed; loss curve slower for the first 100 steps then crossing below baseline; validation loss down 0.02 to 0.04.
test: A 3-step timing and VRAM check first (fail if over 9.5s or over 5.6 GB); then 45 matched steps; then 3 seeds. Control: the same loop without per-pass logits, to attribute the gain.
target: residual RMS growth, flatter across the 18 effective layers
breaks: A block's weights are applied exactly once per forward pass.
keeps: Twelve unique blocks, all branch weights, the four-stream residual, Muon and AdamW grouping.
kill: Train loss at step 45 more than 0.06 nats above baseline, or step time over 9.5s.

idea: Paired MLP sharing funds eighteen blocks
mechanism: At 2.4 tokens per parameter the MLPs are the undertrained knowledge stores and attention is cheap in parameters; share each MLP between two adjacent blocks (nine unique MLPs) and spend the saved 7.4M parameters on six more blocks with their own attention, norms and routing. Each shared MLP gets twice the gradient signal per token, and sequence mixing gets 18 unique layers instead of 12.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters about 21.8M (under the cap); step time about 1.4x with eight of the eighteen blocks checkpointed; peak VRAM under baseline; validation loss down 0.02 to 0.05.
test: Build-only parameter count, then 3-step timing and VRAM, then 45 matched steps. Control: eighteen blocks with twelve unique MLPs cycled, to separate the sharing effect from the depth effect.
breaks: Depth and parameter count move together because no block reuses weights.
keeps: One attention and one MLP stage per block, pre-norm, four-stream mixing, tied head.
kill: Train loss at step 45 more than 0.06 nats above baseline, or parameter count over 23.37M.

mechanism: Attention entropy in the deepest layers is typically near uniform while early attention does the hard mixing, so move attention budget down the stack: blocks 0 to 2 get a second attention stage (with its own read and write logits), blocks 10 and 11 drop attention and become MLP-only. Net 13 attention stages and 12 MLP stages instead of 12 and 12.
prediction: Parameters up 0.59M; step time up about 2% plus 2% for checkpointing block 0; peak VRAM within baseline after that checkpoint; validation loss down 0.01, lost entirely if deep attention is not redundant.
test: First print per-layer attention entropy in a 200-step baseline smoke; if the last two blocks are not the highest-entropy layers, drop the idea. Then 45 matched steps, then 3 seeds.
target: attention entropy in deep layers, removed where it is near uniform
breaks: Every block has the same attention-then-MLP stage layout.
keeps: Twelve blocks, all stage internals, the four-stream residual, parameter count near baseline.
kill: Train loss at step 45 more than 0.03 nats above baseline.

idea: Dense depth read over block means
mechanism: DenseFormer's depth-weighted averaging, placed where this recipe already has a softmax read: each stage's read softmax ranges over its four current streams plus one logit per earlier block's stream mean, initialised at minus six so the function starts as the baseline. Late layers can then read early states directly instead of through the mixing chain, which is the interaction with multi-stream mixing the brief lists as open.
prediction: About 150 added parameters; step time up 3 to 8% from small adds; no added peak memory because earlier block states are already saved by autograd; validation loss down 0.01 to 0.02 and a flatter gradient norm across depth.
test: 3-step timing to confirm the add overhead, then 45 matched steps, then 3 seeds. Inspect learned logits: if no block puts more than 5% weight on a non-adjacent block, the mechanism is unused.

mechanism: The parameter headroom is 1.16 blocks and the baseline is parameter-starved relative to its data; add a thirteenth block and checkpoint blocks 0 and 1 so the extra activations fit in the 0.1 GB of free memory.
prediction: Parameters up 1.83M (under the cap); step time up about 12%; peak VRAM at or below baseline; validation loss down 0.005 to 0.01.
test: Build-only count, 3-step timing and VRAM, then 3 seeds. Range: 13 (candidate) and 11 (control, to confirm loss is still falling with depth at this size).

mechanism: Residual RMS grows with depth under pre-norm so deep blocks contribute less relative to the stream, the Curse-of-Depth mechanism; initialise each block's write logits so its write weight starts at c divided by the square root of the block index plus one, matching LayerNorm Scaling but applied to the write rather than the norm so attention and MLP keep their input scale.
prediction: No parameter or time change; residual RMS at block 11 relative to block 0 falls from the baseline's measured ratio; validation loss down 0.005 if deep layers were under-contributing, zero otherwise.
test: Print per-block residual RMS in a 200-step baseline smoke; if growth is under 1.5x the idea has nothing to fix. Sweep c in {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} over 45 matched steps, then 3 seeds on the best.

idea: Normalize the row before it enters the stream
mechanism: Anomaly row restated: block-0 MLP gradient is 0.0718 above what layers 1 and 2 predict on all three seeds. Rival causes: (a) the embedding enters at RMS 0.02 while block 0 writes at RMS 1.4, so block 0 is the real embedding and MLP-0 is a bigram table; (b) a training-phase effect, at step 100 only shallow layers learn and the excess vanishes by step 500; (c) a measurement artifact, raw gradient norm under pre-norm scales as one over the residual RMS at that depth and layer 0 sits where RMS is smallest, so the neighbour extrapolation is wrong. Five-minute probe on the step-100 checkpoint: multi
prediction: Block-0 attention and MLP gradient norms fall toward the layer 1-2 trend; the residual RMS after block 0 rises from 1.4 to about 2; the loss curve is ahead by 0.05 to 0.10 nats at step 100 and val loss ends 0.008 to 0.015 lower. Params plus 384, step time unchanged.
test: 100-step smoke on seed 0 against the recorded curve; kill if step-100 loss is not at least 0.03 below 6.179 and the layer-0 excess has not halved. Fallback sweep in TEST of the tune below.
target: gradient norm spread, down (layer 0 toward trend); residual RMS growth, down

idea: Fixed input scale on the tied row
mechanism: The same cause as above with no norm: multiply the looked-up row by a fixed constant before the broadcast so the input is not 70x smaller than block 0's write. Keeps row norm visible to the input, which the norm port removes, so the two together tell whether row norm carries useful frequency signal into the stream.
prediction: Same direction as the norm port but smaller, val 0.003 to 0.008 lower at the best constant, worse than baseline at 50 or more once rows for frequent tokens grow. Params and step time unchanged.

mechanism: Rerepresented as a predictive coder, each block's branch adds the innovation the stream does not already carry; the natural edit is that an innovation is orthogonal to the current state. In the code, the component of the MLP output along the unit-normalised input direction only rescales the stream, which every later pre-norm removes, so w_down spends capacity on a direction that changes only later layers' sensitivity, not their input. Storing gate and up as one fused matrix makes Muon orthogonalise them jointly, so the gate update and the up update share one orthonormal input basis instead of being free to learn the same input direction twice in a step; the per-entry update RMS is unchanged by the shape-aware scale, so only the coupling changes, and one GEMM replaces two.

idea: Reachable mixing: mix logit init 6 to 2
mechanism: With logits at 6 the Sinkhorn plan is 99.75% identity, and under AdamW at 3e-3 over 1526 steps with decoupled decay the logits can move by at most about 4, so the plan stays at least 94% identity for the whole budget: the 20 Sinkhorn iterations per stage are paid for a matrix that is frozen at the identity by its own init. Starting at 2 (plan 70% identity, 10% per off-diagonal) puts the mixing inside the region the optimiser can shape within the budget; it only pays off when streams differ, so it is meant to be tested together with the staggered-write port above.

idea: Signed writes: streams hold sums and differences of attention and MLP outputs
mechanism: Rerepresented as an ODE across depth, the state is x' = a(x) + m(x) and the four streams are four integrators of the same flow; the edit natural in that form is to integrate a and m with opposite signs on some streams, which the code forbids because its gains are 2·sigmoid. Replace the write gain with 2·tanh and initialise the attention stage to [+1, +1, +1, -1] and the MLP stage to [+1, +1, -1, +1], so stream 2 holds emb + A - M and stream 3 holds emb - A + M. A convex read of the four streams can then produce emb + αA + βM for any α, β in the hull, including the raw embedding (α=β=0), an MLP
prediction: Learned read logits leave uniform within 200 steps (baseline reads have no gradient because the streams are copies); loss at 50M tokens 0.01 nats lower, mostly on rare tokens via the embedding-only read; parameters and time unchanged.
test: 45 matched steps; then at a 300-step checkpoint check that at least one block's read vector lies off the (1,1) corner of the hull by more than 0.3. 3 seeds at 50M.

idea: A stream that integrates along positions
mechanism: Rerepresented as a PDE, the residual flows across depth but is frozen along the sequence except where attention moves it, and the measured layer 0 spends its attention computing a near-uniform context average (entropy 0.957). The edit natural in that form is a diffusion term along positions: stream 3 receives, instead of the branch, the causal running mean of the branch over positions (one float32 cumsum of B×T×384 per stage, divided by position count), so every block and the head see, at 1/4 weight through the mean read, a prefix summary that no attention head has to spend its budget on. idea: Angular step: write gain proportional to the RMS of the state read
mechanism: In ODE form the measured linear RMS growth (1.4 to 10.9) means a constant step added to a state whose norm grows, so the angle each layer turns the state shrinks like 1/depth: layer 0 rotates it fully, layer 11 by a tenth, which matches the tenfold gradient decay across depth. The natural edit is a step size proportional to the state norm: the write gain becomes 2·sigmoid(w)·RMS(read state), detached, with w initialised so the factor is 0.15, so every stage adds the same relative amount and the state grows geometrically (about 28x) instead of linearly, giving late layers the same leverage as e
prediction: Gradient norm spread across blocks 1 to 11 falls from 1.7x to under 1.3x; residual growth becomes geometric; loss at 50M tokens 0.005 to 0.01 nats lower or, if early-layer contributions get drowned, higher; no parameter or time change.

idea: Leapfrog split of the four streams
mechanism: Rerepresented as a Hamiltonian system, streams 0-1 are the position q and streams 2-3 the momentum p; attention reads p and writes q, the MLP reads q and writes p (read logits init +3 on its half, write gains 1.9 on its half and 0.05 on the other). Each branch then sees the embedding plus the accumulated outputs of the other kind only, each half receives 12 writes instead of 24, and the two halves stay bounded separately; the softmax reads and the Sinkhorn leak let the model reopen a direct attention-to-attention path if it needs it for induction.
prediction: Residual RMS growth halves; recall-token loss worsens at first (induction composition is indirect) and must recover by step 300; loss at 50M tokens 0.005 nats lower or worse; parameters and time unchanged.

breaks: Every branch reads and writes the same averaged state; here attention and MLP each read the other's accumulated outputs.
keeps: Four streams, static doubly-stochastic mixing, token-independent reads, mean at the head, same parameter count.

mechanism: After derotation, multiply the rotated and unrotated halves of each head's output by separate query-dependent sigmoid gates. Diffuse heads can then shut off their cancelled rotated half, and sharp heads can use it.

mechanism: Drop "K/V at t depend only on x_t". Use latent = norm(W_c x_t ⊙ silu(W_g x_{t−1})), with x_{t−1} a causal shift by one position and zero at t=0. The KV code then directly carries "which token preceded me", which is the key an induction head matches on.

mechanism: Keep one 128-dim normed latent c. Each head h gets its own gate g_h = 2·sigmoid(W_h c) through a single 128→768 map (98k params per layer, 1.18M total, within headroom), and `expand` acts per head on c ⊙ g_h. This lets the six heads read different subsets of the shared code.

mechanism: In the optimiser, rescale each `tok.weight` row's Adam update to a fixed RMS, so rare rows that get small, consistent gradients move at the same per-row rate as frequent rows.
prediction: Lower rank 1000–10000 band loss at step 100.
test: 100 matched steps against baseline.

idea: Counted bias plus μ-centering of output directions
mechanism: Combine the counted bias and direction-only head with μ-centering: subtract the mean normalised row after each step, so the common push-down direction the bias now carries cannot reappear in the rows.
prediction: Anisotropy near 0 with no loss cost, and a slightly larger gain on the mid bands.
test: 45-step matched run against the direction-only arm.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

mechanism: Because the stream mean contains exactly e_x, read out `norm(x.mean(2) − tok(idx))`. The tied head then never scores the current token by its own embedding and only sees what the blocks wrote.
prediction: The current token's own logit drops toward the mean, and repetition errors fall. Loss either drops a little or rises if the blocks relied on the copy.
test: 45-step matched run against baseline.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
breaks: The readout sees the full residual stream, including the input embedding.
kill: Steps 30–45 mean loss more than 0.01 above baseline.

mechanism: Drop "offset rides on rotated value dims". Append one value dim per head holding log(1+j) and subtract log(1+i) from that output dim after SDPA, so each head reports its attention-weighted mean log-position minus its own. This is linear and has no phase cancellation. Feed the 6 extra dims into `wo` (+2304 params per layer).
prediction: Lower loss than baseline from step 1, unaffected by attention diffuseness; earlier induction formation in the repeated-random-token probe.
test: Formation-step sweep (Q8) on baseline vs this; kill if formation is not earlier by ≥ 20% of steps.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm

mechanism: Multiply the value-rotation angles by s(t) ramping 0→1 between steps 150 and 450. Early training sees identity values with no cancellation cost; the offset phase appears once attention has sharpened.
prediction: No loss penalty at step 45/100 relative to baseline; recall-token loss below baseline after step 450.
test: Matched 600-step runs with the recall split and repeated-random probe at step 600.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm
breaks: The positional encoding is fixed from step 0 and does not change during training.
kill: At step 600, repeated-random in-context gain not ≥ 0.1 nat above baseline, or total loss > baseline + 0.01.

idea: Rotary values only in layers 1–3, mid band
mechanism: Rotate only the k = 3..10 band (16 dims) and only in layers 1–3. The offset-coded output feeds later layers' keys (K-composition) and can stand in for a previous-token head; the low-entropy late layers keep clean values.
prediction: Induction formation step earlier than baseline; non-recall loss unchanged.
test: Formation sweep at steps 100/200/400 vs baseline, 1 seed each first.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm

mechanism: Mix x_{t−1} into the normed attention input through a learned per-channel gate (RWKV token shift). Previous-token information then exists in layer 0 without a previous-token head, and induction becomes one-layer.
prediction: Repeated-random in-context gain appears within the first 200 steps; the recall split improves at step 100.
test: 100-step matched smoke plus the repeated-random probe.
part: Input embedding / block input

mechanism: Add a learned null key/value per head (softmax off-by-one). Diffuse heads can then park mass on the sink instead of spreading it over many tokens, which reduces phase cancellation in the rotated slice.
prediction: The L2 ratio (RMS of rotated / unrotated output) rises in layers 0–2 compared with rotation alone.
test: L2 ratio at step 100, rotation vs rotation + sink.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm

mechanism: Give all four streams distinct write-logit patterns (stream = stage index mod 4 favoured, ±0.5) and slightly distinct read logits. This removes the exact 2↔3 clone and gives the mixing real differences to act on.
prediction: Streams 2 and 3 are no longer bit-identical at step 20, and the spread ratio at block 11 is at least 5x the current value at step 100.
test: A 20-step smoke run checking `torch.equal(x[:,:,2], x[:,:,3])` and the spread ratio.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Replace Sinkhorn with M = J/4 + P_⊥ R P_⊥, where R is the Cayley transform of a zero-initialised skew 3×3 on the zero-mean subspace. The mean is kept exactly, differences are rotated without shrinking, negative entries are allowed, and no iterations are needed.
prediction: The spread ratio does not decay with depth, and step time drops measurably.
test: A 100-step smoke run comparing the spread ratio by layer and the loss at matched steps against the current script.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Use exact identity, skipping the einsum, at 21 of the 24 stages, and apply a learned mix at init 3 only after blocks 3, 7 and 11. This cuts kernel launches and the per-stage bf16 rounding of the residual while keeping some exchange.
prediction: Step time drops by 5% or more, and loss is unchanged within noise.
test: `--smoke-steps 50`, comparing tok/s and `loss_curve`.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Replace `x.mean(dim=2)` with softmax(final_read) weights initialised to zeros. The step-0 forward is identical, but stream-specific writes can now reach the logits.
prediction: The final read weights leave 0.25 by more than 0.05 by step 300, with a small loss change at matched steps.
test: A 300-step smoke run logging the final read weights.
part: Output readout (final norm and tied head)

idea: Embedding stream via the clone slot
mechanism: Turn stream 3, currently a clone of stream 2, into an embedding-only stream: write gain fixed at 0 and its row and column of M pinned to identity. Every read can then mix in x0, as with the modded-nanogpt embedding skip.
prediction: Read weight on stream 3 rises above 0.25 in some blocks; loss at matched step 100 is equal or lower.
test: A 100-step smoke run on 2 seeds comparing read weights and the loss curve.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

idea: Routed writes (one stream per layer group)
mechanism: Block l writes only into stream l mod 4, with gain 0 elsewhere and identity mixing. The streams become a structured memory of layer groups that the softmax reads select from, similar to a rank-4 DenseFormer. A learned final read replaces the mean.
prediction: Strong stream specialisation (spread ratio above 0.5), and reads in late blocks put their weight on specific groups.
test: A 100-step smoke run against the current script with the same seed.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing
breaks: Every layer writes into every stream with gain near 1.
kill: Step-100 loss more than 0.08 nats above the current script, averaged over 2 seeds.

mechanism: Drop "offset must ride in value phase". Append one scalar j/T to each head's value (SDPA allows v width ≠ q/k width), then compute i/T − y_extra = the attention-weighted mean offset. Feed it through log1p into a tiny per-head linear into the head output before `wo`.
prediction: Offset information reaches the residual stream without cancelling content. Non-recall loss unchanged at step 100; final val loss −0.003 to −0.01.
test: 45-step matched smoke for non-recall loss parity, plus a probe of the mean-offset feature's per-layer variance (it should differ from 0.5·i/T in layers ≥4).
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm
breaks: values carry only content; position never enters the read vector
kill: at step 100, total loss above baseline by >0.01, or step time >+5%

idea: Long-wavelength-only value rotation in sharp layers
mechanism: Rotate only the 8 slowest-useful frequencies (k=3..10, wavelengths ≈35–1990) on 16 value dims, and only in layers 6–11, where entropy is ≈0.67–0.71. Cancellation is then small and the phase stays decodable.
prediction: The RMS ratio of rotated to unrotated output is ≥0.6 in layers 6–11. The non-recall loss rise seen with the full version disappears.
test: 45-step smoke measuring the per-layer RMS ratio and non-recall loss against baseline.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm

mechanism: Force one of layer 0's six heads to attend only to position i−1 (with i at t=0) via a fixed mask. The prerequisite of induction is then present from step 0, and the diffuse layer 0 gets one sharp head.
prediction: Repeated-random gain crosses 1 nat earlier than baseline. The anomalous layer-0 gradient (0.29) moves toward ~0.04.
test: Probe script with checkpoints every 100 steps for 3 seeds; compare onset steps.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm
breaks: every head learns its attention pattern freely
kill: at step 100, total loss above baseline by >0.02

mechanism: Port the "earlier induction" goal to the part "Optimizer: Muon/AdamW grouping". Give `wq`, `rotary` and `compress` a separate Muon group at 1.5x lr, so sharp positional heads form sooner within the budget.
prediction: Minimum layer entropy at step 300 is below the baseline's; final val loss −0.003 to −0.008.
test: 100-step smoke logging per-layer entropy and loss against baseline.
part: Optimizer: Muon/AdamW grouping

mechanism: Add modded-nanogpt's gated smear, x_t += σ(g)·x_{t−1} on embeddings. Previous-token identity is then present without a learned head, which leaves attention free to use offset-aware values for induction-like copies.
prediction: Earlier repeated-random onset than either change alone; recall-token loss down ≥0.03 at step 300.
test: 2×2 matched 300-step smoke (baseline / rotate / smear / both) with the recall split.
part: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm

mechanism: Drop the assumption "the scalars share the decayed group with a target of 0". Keep the per-channel vectors but parameterize them as 1+w, so AdamW's decay pulls toward identity instead of toward 0.68x shrinkage.
prediction: End-state gain mean near 1 with CV near the noise floor, and loss equal to or slightly better than baseline. Parameter count unchanged.
test: A 500-step paired run. Compare the gain mean (baseline expected below 0.9 from decay) and the matched loss.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

mechanism: Replace the q_norm gain with 6 per-head scalars stored as log τ, exempt from decay, initialized to log 1.4. Multiplicative Adam steps let each head set its own sharpness.
prediction: Head temperatures spread out by step 500 (some above 2, some below 1). Attention entropy falls in layers 3–11.
test: A 300-step run logging the 72 temperatures. If all stay within ±10% of 1.4, the per-head freedom is unused.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

idea: Collapse gains to their mean at cooldown start
mechanism: At step 1,067, overwrite every gain vector with its mean and freeze the spread (keep only a scalar from then on). This tests whether the accumulated per-channel spread carries information in the late phase.
prediction: If the spread is noise, there is no loss jump at step 1,068 and the final val is equal or better. If it encodes features, the loss jumps and does not recover.
test: Paired seeds. Compare step 1,068–1,080 train loss with baseline.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati
breaks: Gains learned throughout keep their per-channel spread to the end.
kill: Mean train loss over steps 1,068–1,080 more than 0.02 above paired baseline.

idea: Input-embedding scalar to fix the tiny layer-0 stream
mechanism: Put one learned scalar (no decay, init about 10) on the token embedding before it is expanded into the 4 streams, so the raw stream RMS is not about 0.02 against a 1.4–10.9 residual.
prediction: The layer-0 attention gradient falls from 0.24 toward the 0.02–0.03 band, and early loss improves.
test: A 45-step smoke logging per-layer attention gradient norms.
part: Residual streams: embedding input and stream initialization

idea: Scalar temperatures with nGPT's scale reparameterization
mechanism: Store each scalar as p with effective value p·(s_init/s_scale), as nGPT does for its scaling factors. This sets Adam's effective step on the temperature independently of the global lr_adam.
prediction: Temperatures move about 3x slower or faster as chosen. Removes early overshoot of the 1.4x q-scale during warmup.
test: A 100-step run comparing the scalar trajectories and attention max-logit with the plain-scalar build.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

mechanism: Drop "all rows share one table". The head uses `cat(E[:, :368], U)` with U of size 50304×16 as an output-only parameter, while the input still reads all 384 dimensions of E. This gives a small private channel to the output side for frequency and anisotropy.
prediction: Non-embedding parameters reach about 22.05M; loss beats bias-only at steps 200–300 as the output prior moves into U.
test: 300 schedule-matched steps (`--smoke-seconds`) on 3 paired seeds against bias-only.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
breaks: Full tying of every dimension.
kill: Paired mean of `loss_curve[199:300]` not below bias-only by at least 0.01 on all 3 seeds.

mechanism: Also RMS-normalise the input lookup and multiply it by a separate per-token input scale. Row norm then carries no meaning anywhere, and the two roles get two independent scalar vectors.
prediction: Spearman correlation between row norm and log frequency drops below 0.2 by step 100; layer-0 attention gradient falls toward layer-1 levels.
test: 100 paired steps; log the layer-0 grad norm and the norm/frequency Spearman correlation.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

idea: Training-wheel counted prior, faded out by step 300
mechanism: A frozen counted log-unigram buffer is added to the logits with weight λ(t), going from 1 to 0 linearly over steps 0–300. The prior is used only in the phase where it helps, and the final model's forward is plain.
prediction: A 1–3 nat gain at steps 1–10, and no loss jump as λ reaches 0 if the rows have absorbed the prior.
test: Compare paired `loss_curve` slopes around step 300 against baseline.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
breaks: The logit function is fixed throughout training.
kill: Loss at steps 300–350 more than 0.01 above paired baseline.

mechanism: Replace `expand(-1, -1, 4, -1)` with per-token 4-vector weights (50304×4, initialised to 1) so token identity chooses which Sinkhorn streams it enters, moving per-token salience out of row norm.
prediction: Mid-frequency band (rank 100–10k) loss falls by at least 0.01 at step 300.
test: 300 paired steps with a band-wise probe.
part: Residual streams: Sinkhorn mixing and read/write weights

idea: Direction-only head with lazy row decay
mechanism: Combine the direction-only head with LazyAdam-style sparse decay (https://www.tensorflow.org/addons/api_docs/python/tfa/optimizers/LazyAdam): decay is applied only to rows looked up in the current batch, so rare rows stop shrinking on every step while their output direction stays intact.
prediction: Rank-10k+ band loss falls by at least 0.02 compared with direction-only.
test: 300 paired steps, band-wise probe.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

mechanism: Drops "absolute write RMS matters". Scale the MLP write to exp(a)·ema(block-input stream RMS)/ema(write RMS), so each layer contributes a learned, fixed fraction of the stream it writes into, whatever the stream's size.
prediction: The per-layer write/stream ratio holds at exp(a) within 2x; late layers keep a share comparable to early layers instead of falling as roughly 1/depth.
test: 100-step run; log write/stream ratio per layer; compare loss at steps 40–45.

breaks: a block's write magnitude is independent of how large the stream already is

mechanism: Keep a detached EMA of per-channel RMS (384 values) of the MLP write, with a learned 384-vector log-gain, so outlier channels cannot dominate the RMSNorm reads downstream.
prediction: Max/median channel RMS of the stream drops by at least 2x; +4.6k parameters.
test: 100-step run; log the channel-RMS max/median ratio at layers 0, 6 and 11.
part: Per-token computation: SwiGLU MLP

mechanism: Run AGC only during the first 10% of steps, when relative updates are around 15% per step, then freeze c, multiply it into `w_down.weight`, and remove the scaling, leaving the exam architecture unchanged.
prediction: Lower loss variance across seeds over steps 0–150; final loss at least equal to baseline.
test: Two 200-step runs with 3 seeds each; compare per-step loss standard deviation over steps 0–150.
part: Per-token computation: SwiGLU MLP

mechanism: The same detached EMA gain on the attention branch output, targeting layer 0, where attention gradients are about 10x their neighbours' (z 7.0).
prediction: The layer-0 attention gradient anomaly shrinks below 3x its neighbours' predicted value.
test: 100-step run on 3 seeds; recompute the layer-0 gradient anomaly.

idea: AGC plus a fixed-norm (hyperspherical) MLP matrix projection
mechanism: After each Muon step, project w_gate, w_up and w_down back to their initial Frobenius norms (as nGPT keeps weights normalized), so the gain a alone sets magnitude and the radial ratchet from A2 cannot occur.
prediction: MLP ||W|| constant by construction; ||dw||/||w|| spread at most x1.3; loss at steps 40–45 no worse than baseline.
test: 100-step run; compare update spread and the loss window against plain AGC.
part: Per-token computation: SwiGLU MLP

mechanism: The token embedding enters the stream at RMS about 0.02, while block 0 writes about 1.4. Scale the input copy of `tok(idx)` by exp(a)/ema so the embedding keeps a learned share of the stream; the tied head is left untouched.
prediction: Loss on tokens of rank 1000–50304 (38% of tokens, losses 8.98 and 11.61) falls by at least 0.05 nats at step 100.
test: 100-step run; compare per-frequency-bucket loss against the measured baseline buckets.
part: Token embedding
breaks: the embedding enters the stream at its raw learned scale
kill: mean loss over steps 40–45 more than 0.03 nats above baseline, or rank-0–100 loss more than 0.05 nats worse at step 100

idea: Weightless foldable norms, one content temperature per layer
mechanism: Make n1, n2 and latent_norm fully weightless, since their gains fold into the following Linear layers. Replace q_norm and k_norm gains with one no-decay scalar τ_l per layer on the content logits. Keep the final 384-wide gain until Q6 is settled.
prediction: Params −11,099 + 384 kept = about −10,715. Step-45 loss within ±0.02 of baseline. τ_l rises above 1 in mid and late layers.
test: Run `--build-only` and check the delta, then a 45-step smoke paired on seed 0.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati
breaks: Every normalization owns a learnable scale.
kill: Mean train loss over steps 36–45 more than 0.03 above baseline.

idea: Separate per-head content and rotary temperatures
mechanism: Put two no-decay scalars per head on the SDPA logits, one multiplying q_c and one multiplying q_r. Init content at 1.4 and rotary at 1.0. These are the only attention scales that Muon and the shared head-wide gains cannot set per head.
prediction: By step 300 the per-head temperatures diverge (spread > 0.2 within a layer). Attention entropy at layers 3–11 falls by 0.01–0.08.
test: A 300-step run logging the temperature trajectories. Equal per-head values refute the need.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

idea: Keep gains only where the evidence says they work: layer-0 n1 and the final norm
mechanism: Use scalars everywhere except layer-0 n1 (the anomalous 0.24 gradient) and the final norm (the tied-head decoupling), which keep their 384-wide gains.
prediction: Params about −8.8k. The rare-token bucket shows no regression at step 100.
test: Run the step-100 matched loss split by frequency bucket against the full-scalar version.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

idea: Learned scalar on the embedding stream input
mechanism: Multiply `tok(idx)` by one no-decay scalar initialized so the 4-stream input RMS is about 1, instead of std 0.02. This targets the tiny raw-embedding stream that is the likely cause of the 7× layer-0 gradient.
prediction: The layer-0 attention gradient ratio drops from about 10× toward 2×. Step-100 loss is within ±0.02 or better.
test: A 100-step smoke logging per-layer attention gradient norms.
part: Embedding / input stream
breaks: The embedding enters the residual stream at its init scale (std 0.02) with no separate learned gain.
kill: Step-45 matched loss more than 0.03 above baseline, or layer-0 gradient ratio not below 5×.

mechanism: Parametrize each scalar as c·(1 + w) with w = 0 at init and normal wd 0.1. Decay then pulls toward the chosen temperature c (1.4 for attention, 1.0 elsewhere) instead of toward zero, so `build_optimizers` needs no edit.
prediction: End-of-run scalars stay within 0.7–1.5 of c. The final loss matches the no-decay variant within 0.005.
test: A 500-step run comparing scalar trajectories against the plain-scalar build.
part: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati

idea: Partial tie with a private output subspace
mechanism: Drop "the classifier is the whole input row". The head uses [E_v ; P_v], where P is a private 50304×32 output-only block. P is fed by a 384→32 projection of the normed read-out (about 1.6M parameters, so about 22.85M, under the 23.36M cap). Output-shaped features (frequency, next-token-class) can live in P, so the shared 384 dimensions stop being dragged toward the output geometry.
prediction: Layer-0 attention gradient falls from 0.24–0.29 toward the layer-1 level, the mid-frequency bands improve, and the training loss gap opens after step 100.
test: A 45-step `--smoke-seconds` paired run, 3 seeds, plus a layer-0 gradient readout.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
breaks: The full-row tie between input lookup and output classifier.
kill: mean(loss_curve[29:45]) is not below baseline by at least 3× the measured A/A floor and at least 0.01 nats on 3 seeds.

mechanism: The input lookup also uses RMS-normalized rows times its own per-token input gain (a further 50304 scalars), separate from the output scale. The table becomes pure direction on both sides. Under weight decay it becomes scale-invariant, which raises its effective learning rate (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08419).
prediction: Rank-10k+ band loss falls further than with output-only normalization, and the Spearman correlation of row norm with frequency becomes meaningless, replaced by the correlation of the gains with frequency.
test: A 45-step paired run against the direction-only arm on the rank-10k+ band.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

mechanism: Put the table in its own AdamW group with wd = 0. After each step, decay only the rows whose gradient row norm is nonzero: `p[rows] *= 1 − lr·wd`. A rare row seen once every 50 steps then decays once rather than 50 times between updates.
prediction: Rare-row norms stay near init, and rank-10k+ band loss falls by at least 0.05 nats at step 100 with no change at rank 0–100.
test: Row-norm histogram by frequency band at step 100, plus band losses, paired.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

mechanism: Replace `x.mean(dim=2)` in the head with softmax(read_out_logits) over the 4 streams. The logits are zero-init, so step 0 equals the mean. The head can then weight the streams that carry output-ready content instead of always including the raw e_x share.
prediction: The read-out weights move away from uniform within 200 steps, and loss improves by 0.005–0.02.
test: Track the read-out weights at steps 45 and 200, plus a paired 45-step loss comparison.
part: Stream read-out

idea: Direction-only head plus chunked fp32 cross-entropy
mechanism: Combine with Cut Cross-Entropy-style chunking (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.09009). Compute logits and loss in fp32 over chunks of 1024 tokens (about 206 MB per chunk), so the bias b and scale s act at fp32 resolution instead of the 0.0625 bf16 step near logit 10. Chunking also lowers peak VRAM compared with the full 412 MB bf16 logits.
prediction: The rare-band gain from s and b grows, the peak VRAM report falls, and the A/A floor may shrink.
test: A 3-step smoke for memory and time, then a paired 45-step run against bf16 logits.
part: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits

mechanism: Moving `read_logits` and `write_logits` from Muon to AdamW (lr 3e-3, wd 0) replaces fixed-size normalised steps with Adam's per-element signal-to-noise scaling, so gates drift only when the gradient has a consistent sign.
prediction: Read |w−0.25| stays below 0.02 by step 100 when the gradient is noise; the loss is equal or slightly better.
test: 100-step smoke for both optimiser placements on 2 seeds; compare read deviation and step-100 train loss.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Parameterise writes as 4·softmax(write_logits) so the total write into the mean stays exactly 4, and init the favoured logit at +2, rotating which stream is favoured with (2·layer+stage) mod 4. Streams then differ by O(1) instead of 2%, and all four get used.
prediction: Block-11 spread ratio is at least 0.3 at step 100; mean-stream RMS is within 3% of control; the read gradient is consistent (update cosine above 0.5).
test: 100-step smoke logging spread ratio and update cosine.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Hold `read_logits` and `write_logits` at their init for the first 150 steps (the warmup plus early phase, when stream differences are mostly rounding) and unfreeze them afterwards, so Muon cannot lock in noise-driven read biases early.
prediction: End read deviation is lower and more consistent across seeds; exam loss matches or beats control.
test: 3-seed full run compared with control on the across-seed spread of final read weights.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Replace `x.mean(dim=2)` before the final norm with a learned softmax read over streams (4 params, AdamW), so the head can choose the stream that the writes have specialised.
prediction: The output read leaves uniform only if streams specialise; zero parameter cost.
test: 100-step smoke checking output-read deviation alongside step-100 loss.
part: Output head readout

idea: Dynamic read on top of static Sinkhorn
mechanism: Add the dynamic-HC per-token read term tanh(norm(x)·W)·s, with W of shape d×4 per stage and s initialised to 0, to the static read logits. This adds 384·4·24 ≈ 37k parameters, within C3.
prediction: The dynamic term gives token-dependent stream selection, the part where dynamic HC beat static HC (2.781 vs 2.791 on OLMo-1B).
test: 3-seed full run against the static-read control.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing

mechanism: Replace softmax reads with unconstrained linear read weights initialised to 0.25 (AdamW, no decay), so a read can take x_i − x_j and the four streams act as a difference-carrying memory instead of a convex average.
prediction: Some stages learn negative weights; the exam loss improves if streams carry distinct content.
test: 100-step smoke against control.
part: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing
breaks: reads are convex combinations summing to 1
kill: step-100 train loss more than 0.02 above control, or any stage with |Σw| > 1.5

mechanism: Drops the assumption that attention count must change. Keep 12 attention + 12 MLP stages but order them A,A,A,M | (A,M)×9 | M,M,M across 12 blocks, i.e. stage counts per block (A,A) (A,M)… (M,M). This isolates placement from parameter count.
prediction: Same params and FLOPs as baseline; loss within −0.01 to +0.005.
test: 200-step, 3-seed matched comparison against baseline and against the 13/12 idea; if the 13/12 version wins only by the param delta, placement is not the cause.
part: State across depth: layer count and block layout

mechanism: Train one baseline to completion, zero each attention branch in turn and measure the loss rise on train-shard windows. Remove the two least important attention stages wherever they sit, and duplicate attention in the two most important blocks.
prediction: The removed stages cost under 0.01 nats each in ablation; the final loss beats the fixed 0–2 / 10–11 layout.
test: The ablation sweep itself (12 evaluations on one checkpoint). If no stage costs under 0.02, there is nothing to move.
part: State across depth: layer count and block layout

mechanism: Drop attention only in block 11 and spend its 528,640 params on that block's MLP (d_ff 1077 to about 1536). Nothing is added at the bottom.
prediction: Parameter-neutral; loss change within ±0.005 if top attention is redundant; recall-token loss unchanged.
test: 200 steps on 3 seeds; recall-token loss rising more than 0.05 refutes it.
part: State across depth: layer count and block layout
breaks: Every block has an attention stage.
